title: Fidelity Sees Huge Bitcoin Potential in $150 Trillion Bond Market
summary: Bitcoin-focused preferred stocks could draw more income-seeking capital into cryptocurrency purchases, a new Fidelity analysis suggests. The firm sees room for growth within the $150 trillion global fixed-income market, with investment outcomes tied to bitcoin’s performance and issuer strength. How ...
content:
Bitcoin-focused preferred stocks could draw more income-seeking capital into cryptocurrency purchases, a new Fidelity analysis suggests. The firm sees room for growth within the $150 trillion global fixed-income market, with investment outcomes tied to bitcoin’s performance and issuer strength.

Key Takeaways

  • Fidelity sees bitcoin demand potential in a $150 trillion market.
  • Preferred stocks have financed purchases of 135,979 bitcoin.
  • Strive’s $630 million offering carries a 15% annual dividend rate.

How a $150 Trillion Market Could Fuel Bitcoin Buying

Income-seeking investors could become a larger source of bitcoin demand as companies issue dividend-paying shares to finance purchases. In an analysis published Oct. 20, Zack Wainwright, a research analyst at Fidelity Digital Assets, examined how preferred-stock financing for bitcoin purchases could attract capital from the approximately $150 trillion global fixed-income market.

These securities are preferred equity, with no maturity date, and appeal to investors seeking dividend income. Fidelity estimates the bitcoin-focused preferred-stock segment at approximately $12 billion, illustrating its relatively small size compared with the broader income-investment market. The analysis stated:

“Even modest adoption within the vast fixed income market could materially reshape bitcoin’s supply-demand dynamics, positioning these instruments as a potentially powerful new driver of long-term value.”

Preferred-stock financing supported purchases of 135,979 bitcoin by Oct. 5, including more than 95,000 from March through May. That demand operates against bitcoin’s limited issuance. Fidelity estimates nearly 96% of the maximum supply has already been issued, with the next halving expected in less than two years.

October Offering Expands Bitcoin Treasury Financing

Strive Inc. (Nasdaq: ASST) provided a current example when it closed an offering of its 15% Series A Perpetual SATS Preferred Stock Oct. 20. The company sold 7 million shares at $90 each, generating $630 million in gross proceeds. The SATS shares carry a 15% annual dividend rate calculated on their $100 stated amount.

The SATS financing can support bitcoin purchases, income-producing assets, working capital, and share repurchases. Regular dividend dates begin Nov. 9 and fall on business days, with payments subject to board declarations and legally available funds. The offering broadens the company’s financing options alongside its existing SATA preferred shares.

Strategy Inc. (Nasdaq: MSTR), meanwhile, reported holdings of 848,517 bitcoin after its latest acquisition in an Oct. 19 disclosure. It purchased 267 bitcoin for $22.1 million during the preceding week, using common-stock proceeds and cash. Its latest acquisition illustrates that treasury purchases can draw on several funding sources.

Dividend Costs and Market Conditions Shape Demand

Long-term economics depend on bitcoin appreciation exceeding the cost of the income paid to preferred shareholders. Fidelity cautioned that these instruments carry risks beyond those associated with money market funds. Their performance depends on both the cryptocurrency and the issuing companies.

Recent capital-management activity also shows that preferred-stock financing can move through periods of issuance and repurchases. Strategy disclosed $192.4 million in STRC repurchases Oct. 12, followed by another $193.1 million in its Oct. 19 update. Buying back outstanding shares uses capital that could otherwise serve other treasury purposes.

Its latest preferred-share capacity and liquidity figures showed approximately $17.51 billion available for STRC issuance and sales as of Oct. 18, with no STRC shares sold during the reporting week. Strategy also held a $4.83 billion reserve intended for dividends and interest, plus $447.3 million in cash for broader corporate uses.

title: Switzerland approves first spot Bitcoin ETF for retail investors
summary: BIT Asset Management’s Bitcoin Fund ETF is expected to begin trading on SIX Swiss Exchange in November, with its public offering restricted to Switzerland.
content:
BIT Asset Management’s Bitcoin Fund ETF is expected to begin trading on SIX Swiss Exchange in November, with its public offering restricted to Switzerland.

Switzerland’s financial regulator FINMA has approved the first Swiss-law exchange-traded fund allowing retail investors to gain direct exposure to Bitcoin.

On Thursday, BIT Asset Management said its Bitcoin Fund ETF (BBIT) is expected to begin trading on SIX Swiss Exchange in November. The fund holds Bitcoin directly and is approved for public offering in Switzerland only.

“Most bitcoin products listed in Europe today are exchange-traded products (ETPs), which are debt instruments that carry issuer risk,” said BIT Asset Management.

The Bitcoin Fund ETF is instead a Swiss collective investment scheme, where assets are held separately from those of the fund management company and are “ring-fenced” for investors, it said. 

The fund falls under Switzerland’s “other funds for alternative investments” category with particular risk. FINMA noted that other fund providers have also submitted applications for Bitcoin ETFs. 

While FINMA has allowed funds that invest primarily in a basket of cryptocurrencies since 2021, this is the first time that FINMA has approved a fund that only invests in Bitcoin, citing trading history and higher trading volume compared with other cryptocurrencies.

However, it stressed that Bitcoin remains highly volatile even when accessed through an approved ETF.

title: Bitcoin Bull Score Index Drops From 80 to 60 as Momentum Weakens
summary: Bitcoin’s Bull Score Index has dropped from 80 to 60 since late September, a new analysis shows. The decline signals a slowing trend as the index sits at a threshold the analyst associates with positive momentum. Bitcoin Bull Score Signals Slower Momentum Bitcoin’s market momentum has weakened since...
content:
Bitcoin’s Bull Score Index has dropped from 80 to 60 since late September, a new analysis shows. The decline signals a slowing trend as the index sits at a threshold the analyst associates with positive momentum.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin’s Bull Score Index has fallen 20 points since late September.
  • Analyst views readings above 60 as consistent with positive momentum.
  • Stronger demand and sustained holder profits are needed for progress.

Bitcoin Bull Score Signals Slower Momentum

Bitcoin’s market momentum has weakened since late September, with incoming capital and investor profitability presenting obstacles to further progress. Cryptoquant contributor Darkfost highlighted those conditions in an Oct. 21 assessment of bitcoin’s Bull Score Index on X. BTC was trading at $81,345 at the time of writing.

The analyst stated:

“Since late September, the Bull Score Index has fallen from 80 to 60, signaling a slight slowdown in the trend.”

The index combines 10 indicators covering demand, investor profitability, network activity, and liquidity to assess the market environment. Its earlier increase from 30 to 80 in August reflected eight components turning bullish. That improvement accompanied a price recovery, with spot and futures demand rising together for the first time since early October 2025.

The assessment included a condition for continued positive momentum. The analyst noted:

“Even so, as long as it stays above 60, the overall momentum remains positive.”

Liquidity and Demand Remain Obstacles

Short-term holders, abbreviated as STHs, are among the groups whose profitability the analyst identified as a weakness. This category commonly refers to coins held for fewer than 155 days, a threshold used in Glassnode’s holder classification methodology.

The analyst identified three constraints:

“The main weak points are the lack of incoming liquidity, the growth in bitcoin demand, and the lack of sustained profitability among STHs in particular.”

Buying activity earlier in the recovery varied substantially across wallet sizes, with larger holders accumulating while smaller wallets reduced their balances. Wallets holding at least 100 BTC added approximately 60,000 bitcoin during August. Over the same period, wallets with between 1 and 100 BTC sold roughly 33,000 BTC, while those below 1 BTC shed about 14,000 BTC.

An Oct. 13 analysis of large-holder activity by Cryptoquant placed the Bull Score Index at 80 after a September peak of 90. Researchers described an early bull market in which large investors typically establish positions before retail demand arrives later in the uptrend.

Holder Profitability Shapes the Recovery

Investor profitability also features in broader assessments of how BTC’s market structure is changing as institutional ownership expands. In September, Cryptoquant founder and CEO Ki Young Ju linked moderating market extremes to a larger capital base. His analysis cited rising realized capitalization, which he interpreted as fresh capital entering the market, among the signals supporting his cycle outlook.

Sustained price trends, liquidity, and investor participation help characterize bull and bear market dynamics. Ju’s outlook addresses how institutional ownership could moderate gains and losses across a cycle. Darkfost’s latest comments focus on the immediate improvements needed to support another advance.

The analyst concluded:

“These three conditions still need to improve further before bitcoin can make more progress.”

title: Pentagon bans US forces from using military info to bet in prediction markets
summary: Hegseth warned that prediction market wagers could expose military operations to adversaries.
content:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has barred all Pentagon staff from using undisclosed information to place wagers on upcoming military action, including on prediction market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket. 

In a memo sent to senior Pentagon and defense agencies on Tuesday, Hegseth said all Department of War personnel are prohibited from engaging in financial transactions using nonpublic information. This involves both classified and unclassified information. 

“Make no mistake why this matters. Our enemies watch movements in these markets,” Hegseth wrote. “The lives of our Service members often depend on the enemy not knowing what is coming.”

“Beyond operational security, financial stakes can warp judgment. A logistician with money riding on a strike date has an interest in that date. An analyst with a position on an outcome has an interest in that outcome,” he said. 

The directive follows the April indictment of US Army soldier Gannon Ken Van Dyke, who allegedly used classified information about the operation to capture Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro to make more than $400,000 on Polymarket.

Prosecutors allege Van Dyke participated in planning and executing the operation, then used his advance knowledge to wager on outcomes related to Maduro’s removal. He has pleaded not guilty to all charges.

In February, Israeli authorities arrested and indicted a military reservist and a civilian for allegedly using classified information to place bets on Polymarket related to Israeli military strikes on Iran.

Related: CFTC, US soldier accused of illegal Polymarket bet spar over interpretation of prediction markets

title: VC Giant Andreessen Horowitz Drops ‘Crypto’ Branding From $9.8B Investment Arm
summary: Venture capital powerhouse Andreessen Horowitz is dropping the word “crypto” from the name of its dedicated cryptocurrency investment arm, rebranding the business as a16z Frontier as it expands its focus to artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies. Broadening the Frontier The change, ...
content:
Venture capital powerhouse Andreessen Horowitz is dropping the word “crypto” from the name of its dedicated cryptocurrency investment arm, rebranding the business as a16z Frontier as it expands its focus to artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies.

Key Takeaways

  • Andreessen Horowitz is renaming its crypto investment arm “a16z Frontier,” expanding its focus to AI, robotics, and emerging technologies.
  • The firm has raised nearly $9.8 billion across five crypto funds since 2018, backing Coinbase, Solana, Uniswap, Opensea, and other major projects.
  • Despite dropping “crypto” from its branding, a16z says it will continue investing in blockchain technology, including infrastructure for AI-powered applications.

Broadening the Frontier

The change, announced Thursday by Chris Dixon, the longtime head of a16z Crypto, marks a significant shift in branding for one of the cryptocurrency industry’s most prominent financial backers. But the firm stressed that the move does not signal an exit from digital assets.

“Today we’re announcing that we’re expanding the scope of our new fund beyond crypto startups to the broader category of frontier startups: companies building new technologies and creating markets that may take years to develop,” Dixon wrote. “This is an expansion: We will continue to invest in crypto and related ventures and advocate for sensible crypto regulation.”

The rebranding follows more than a decade of cryptocurrency industry investing by Andreessen Horowitz, which first backed Coinbase in 2013 and established its dedicated a16z Crypto fund in 2018 with $350 million in capital.

Since then, the Silicon Valley investment giant has raised approximately $9.8 billion across five dedicated cryptocurrency funds, making it one of the sector’s largest venture capital investors. That figure represents capital raised for investment rather than money necessarily deployed into companies.

Its fundraising efforts included a $515 million second crypto fund in 2020, a $2.2 billion third fund in 2021, a $4.5 billion fourth fund in 2022, and a $2.2 billion fifth fund announced in May 2026.

Beyond Coinbase, Andreessen Horowitz has backed some of the cryptocurrency industry’s most recognizable companies and projects, including Solana, Uniswap, OpenSea, Anchorage Digital, Alchemy, Avalanche, Optimism, and Phantom. Its investment portfolio spans crypto exchanges, blockchain infrastructure, decentralized finance, digital wallets, and NFT marketplaces.

Dixon argued that the distinction between cryptocurrency companies and traditional technology businesses has become increasingly difficult to draw as blockchain technology spreads into mainstream finance.

“When we started investing in crypto, it was a world of its own,” he wrote. “But as blockchains have become more widely used, the lines have blurred and the infrastructure has gradually receded into the background.”

Andreessen’s Expanding Focus

Under the Frontier branding, the firm plans to pursue a broader range of long-term technology investments, particularly businesses emerging from advances in AI, autonomous machines, robotics, biotechnology, and new computing devices.

Dixon pointed to Andreessen Horowitz’s earlier investments in virtual reality company Oculus and drone startups Skydio and Zipline as examples of its history of backing technologies before they reached widespread adoption. AI will be central to the expanded investment strategy, with Dixon predicting that advances in the technology will enable entirely new products, services, and markets that have yet to be imagined.

He also argued that blockchains could become essential infrastructure for an emerging economy of autonomous AI agents, enabling machine-to-machine payments and new forms of digital coordination.

“Crypto can give new networks native economic capabilities, enable machine-to-machine transactions, and create new ways to bootstrap them,” Dixon wrote.

Dixon will lead a16z Frontier alongside firm founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, as well as general partners Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet. The firm’s existing operational support teams will continue working with portfolio companies on regulatory matters, marketing, recruiting, and technical research.

The rebranding reflects a broader bet that blockchain technology will increasingly become part of the underlying infrastructure of other industries, rather than remain a distinct investment category.

title: The Sleeper Has Awakened: Pepenardo’s Sleeping Knights Return
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

The Sleeper Has Awakened: Pepenardo’s Sleeping Knights Return
Hand-altered magazine covers, one-of-one trading cards, and the evolving culture of bitcoin collectibles.
This post The Sleeper Has Awakened: Pepenardo’s Sleeping Knights Return first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is ...
content:
Pepenardo has transformed six copies of Bitcoin Magazine’s 2036 Issue into original artworks, drawing directly onto the covers with a Sharpie. The hand-altered editions feature familiar characters from his visual universe, including the Sleeping Knights, previously exhibited at the BMAG Museum in Nashville and Bitcoin 2026 in Las Vegas. Other imagery includes the masked rider of FAKEGENESIS, Dorian Nakamoto, and Pepe the Frog.

Each magazine features the artist’s signature on its illustrated cover and an additional gold-ink signature on an interior spread reproducing his painting THE DREAMER. Each is paired with two original, one-of-one trading cards created for the collaboration.

The project reflects BTC Inc.’s growing interest in art, publishing, and collectibles, building on Pepenardo’s MEMETIKRON exhibition at Bitcoin 2026, where THE DREAMER (RED KNIGHT) and THE DREAMLESS (GREEN KNIGHT) became highlights of the BMAG auction.

The two oil paintings, each measuring 30 × 39.5 inches, depict reclining knights in red and green armor, referencing financial markets and historical portraiture. Both sold for 0.32698802 BTC (approximately $26,500 each), attracting a combined 197 bids. Their imagery now reappears in artist-made trading cards featuring alternate colorways, remixed compositions, and hand-painted Creator Rare editions inspired by traditional textiles.

Amid a booming trading card market, Pepenardo’s work bridges painting and handheld collectibles, where scarcity, provenance, and variation shape value. His relationship with this market began well before the Sleeping Knights.

In 2023, his painting FAKEGENESIS, a reinterpretation of Jacques-Louis David’s Napoleon Crossing the Alps featuring a masked rider on a green horse, sold at the Bitcoin Conference in Miami for 1.625 BTC. Originally created as a Fake Rares card in 2022, the composition became an early landmark for physical Bitcoin art, demonstrating the growing collector interest in artwork emerging from Bitcoin’s meme culture.

FAKEGENESIS later appeared on the back cover of Bitcoin Magazine, with prints available through the publication’s store. Its return as a hand-drawn magazine cover completes an unusual progression from trading card to painting, printed reproduction, and original collectible.

Bitcoin Magazine itself has a collecting history dating to its first issue in May 2012, co-founded by Mihai Alisie and Vitalik Buterin. At a bitcoin event in London in September 2012, seven copies of the inaugural issue were signed by more than 20 early bitcoin figures. One attracted a winning bid of 7 BTC, although the buyer never completed the purchase or collected the magazine.

Early issues have since become sought-after historical artifacts, with graded copies and rare editions attracting collectors. In 2023, Bitcoin Magazine introduced the Genesis Box, a limited edition of 21 collector’s sets containing the publication’s first 22 issues, each housed in protective acrylic cases.

Much like early exhibition catalogs, first-edition books, and concert posters, Bitcoin Magazine has developed value beyond its original publishing purpose. Pepenardo’s customized covers extend that history, turning the publication itself into a one-of-one artwork.

I spoke with Pepenardo about his paintings, trading cards, and evolving relationship with Bitcoin Magazine, and with Mark Mason, Head of Media at Bitcoin Magazine, about the historical significance of the publication and its growing collector market.

BMAG: This collaboration came together quickly after you noticed the blank space on the cover of the Bitcoin Magazine issue featuring your work. What inspired you to turn these magazines into original artworks, and how do you see them fitting alongside your paintings and trading cards?

Pepenardo: I couldn’t help but notice that welcoming blank space on the cover. It seemed like an obvious place for a drawing. Coincidentally, I came into Bitcoin through watching the energy around trading cards on Counterparty, from 2016 all the way to the present. Hal Finney foreshadowed this ethos in his famous 1993 email titled “Crypto trading cards.” Of course he was talking about digital collectibles, but the principle stays the same. Bitcoin’s history has a magnetic pull on collectibles; people want to hold on to a fragment of such an important modern history. When we look back fifty years from now, the content and the artifacts that came out of the movement will help future generations make sense of Bitcoin’s tremendous timeline.

BMAG: The two knights, THE DREAMER and THE DREAMLESS, began as oil paintings exhibited and sold at Bitcoin 2026 in Las Vegas. They have since appeared in Bitcoin Magazine and now as original trading cards with different variations. How does the meaning of these characters change as they move between painting, publication, and collectible card? What rules guide your remixed versions, and were you surprised by how quickly the cards sold out?

Pepenardo: I was shocked at how quickly they went. I have no words. But it certainly reinforces that what I’m attempting to create and build with my work has some value. Being able to use the trading cards as a way to remix the original works lets me enrich the life of each painting. The mediums are different – oil on canvas for the paintings, various print methods for the trading cards – but the tedious care that goes into executing both is the same.

BMAG: FAKEGENESIS became a defining work in your career, moving from Fake Rares into an original painting that attracted significant attention at Bitcoin 2023 in Miami. Looking back, what do you remember about that moment, and how did it change your practice and the audience for your work?

Pepenardo: FAKEGENESIS will always be the pivotal work that showed me how I should properly approach my art. I knew that even before it sold. It is a painting that embeds the tropes of Bitcoin’s ethos without being too obvious. Art within the context of Bitcoin shouldn’t have to throw a big B at you all the time; it should give you the fiery sensation of standing inside a new history being built. My hope is that it is remembered as a work that represents an entire movement – onwards and upwards.

BMAG: Bitcoin Magazine’s earliest issues have become historical artifacts in their own right, from signed copies of Issue 1 and graded editions to the Genesis Box collection. Even figures like Michael Saylor have signed covers featuring themselves for charity auctions. What gives these publications their enduring collectible value, and how do you see artist-customized covers like Pepenardo’s fitting into that history?

Mark Mason: For over a decade, Bitcoin Magazine has documented the evolution of Bitcoin, from its early technical developments to the people and culture surrounding it. We see each physical issue as a time capsule, capturing a particular moment in Bitcoin’s journey toward hyperbitcoinization.

One of the biggest factors driving their collectible value is that we never reprint past editions. Each issue has a limited print run, creating a finite supply that has made early editions, graded copies, and signed covers increasingly sought after by collectors.

Bitcoin has always existed at the intersection of technology, economics, and culture. Artist-customized covers like Pepenardo’s take that relationship a step further, transforming an already collectible publication into an original artwork. It’s an extension of what Bitcoin Magazine has become: both a record of Bitcoin’s history and an artifact of that history itself.

Pepenardo’s custom magazine covers and trading card sets sold out shortly after launch, with all six one-of-one editions finding collectors. Additional works remain available, including MASTER CUTS OUT THE STONE (after Hemessen), the centerpiece painting from Pepenardo’s MEMETIKRON exhibition, which traveled from the BMAG Museum in Nashville to Bitcoin 2026 in Las Vegas.

Collectors can also explore FAKEGENESIS prints and the Genesis Box, a limited-edition collector’s set preserving the publication’s first 22 issues from 2012–2014.

The Bitcoin Museum & Art Gallery (BMAG) organizes international exhibitions, auctions, and artist collaborations exploring Bitcoin and its cultural implications. Explore available works from Curtis William Readel’s exhibition Paper Money, along with additional prints, original artworks, and collectibles.

BMAG returns to Bitcoin Amsterdam, November 4–6, 2026, featuring European artists exploring money, power, and Bitcoin. Read more in The Architecture of Money and The Undercurrent. Use code BA26-BMAG20 for discounted admission.

title: New DeepSeek ban in US, Swiss-Asia crypto ties deepen: Asia Express
summary: DeepSeek banned from US federal civilian agencies over spying fears. Singapore firm behind Europe’s only spot Bitcoin ETF, as Switzerland partners with Vietnam on crypto tech.
content:
CHINA

Treasury proposes blocks on US investments in AI and semiconductors in some foreign countries

The US Treasury has proposed new rules that would block investment in artificial intelligence projects (sorry, ‘Super Intelligence’ projects) and certain high risk semiconductors in some foreign countries.

The blocks have been mainly aimed at geopolitical rival China, but will now also encompass other adversaries including Russia, Iran, North Korea and Cuba. The rules would implement the COINS Act from December 2025 and expand the Outbound Investment Security Program that went into effect in January 2025.

They rules build on previous restrictions on selling high powered AI chips to China. The US is backing up its threats too, having announced the first $200,000 penalty this month to Amidi, LLC. Treasury for failing to report an investment by its Chinese subsidiary into embodied AI and robotics company Shanghai Qiongche Intelligent Technology (AKA Noematrix.)

US bans DeepSeek from civilian agency IT systems

The US Department of Homeland Security has ordered the removal of DeepSeek products from federal civilian agency IT systems.

The order, filed on Monday, also covers DeepSeek affiliates and third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations while prohibiting affected agencies from making new purchases.

DHS warned that use of DeepSeek by government employees and contractors could expose sensitive information to China, potentially revealing details about US citizens and federal programs.

Solana’s Liu says Shanghai event postponed over registration surge

The Solana Accelerate event in Shanghai was postponed after pre-registration exceeded the event cap set by local authorities, according to Lily Liu, president of the Solana Foundation.

Event registration quadrupled overnight following publicity for the event, Liu wrote in a Friday X post, adding that organizers decided to postpone the event to “comply with local requirements.”

Earlier on Friday, X users claimed that the event was “abruptly suspended” as law enforcement officers were stationed at the venue.

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao posted he was impressed the Solana Foundation had been allowed to open a Shanghai office, noting than BNB Chain had been unable to do so.

JAPAN

Japan-Korea tourist spending becomes a test case for yen stablecoins

South Korea’s Shinhan Card has signed an agreement with Japan’s SBI VC Trade and SBI XDC Network APAC to test yen stablecoin payments for travelers and cross-border trade settlement.

Under the pact signed Tuesday, the companies will test stablecoin card payments, wallet-to-wallet payments and cross-border trade settlement. They will also assess anti-money-laundering and fraud-detection controls.

Shinhan Card is one of South Korea’s biggest credit card companies. SBI is a Japanese financial heavyweight that runs banks, brokerages, insurers and crypto exchanges.

Metaplanet to take 93.7% stake in Super League through 2,100 BTC deal

Shareholders of Super League, a Nasdaq-listed gaming and digital media company, approved a deal that would give Japanese Bitcoin treasury firm Metaplanet a 93.7% ownership stake, paving the way for its expansion into US capital markets through a publicly traded Bitcoin treasury company.

Metaplanet has also announced a planned repurchase of about $160 million of its own shares.

KOREA

South Korean finance officials met with crypto exchanges amid calls for tax delay

Finance officials reportedly met major crypto exchanges this week, days after a lawmaker introduced legislation that could push the start date of a new crypto tax back two years.

The meeting was a consultation on crypto taxation, with representatives from Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, DigitalX and Gopax, along with executives of the Digital Asset Exchange Alliance, known as DAXA.

South Korean regulators have delayed the crypto tax three times, with the latest delay pushing the start date to 2027 amid political disagreement and industry pushback.

Seoul at night. Source: Pexels, gijecho

Injective, BDACS plan Korean won stablecoin settlement for tokenized assets

Blockchain network Injective has entered into a memorandum of understanding with South Korean digital asset custodian BDACS to bring a won-backed stablecoin to its tokenized asset markets, potentially allowing institutions to settle transactions without relying on US dollar stablecoins.

Kakao plans KRW stablecoin payments ecosystem

Kakao, KakaoBank and KakaoPay have formed a new stablecoin task force to build the infrastructure required for won stablecoin issuance, custody and payments. The aim is to start with shopping and gifting.

MALAYSIA

Malaysia central bank launches DLT platform for tokenized bonds

Malaysia’s central bank has launched a distributed ledger-based platform for issuing and holding tokenized bonds, connecting digital securities records with a payment system designed to operate around the clock. 

Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) said that its next-generation Scripless Securities Depository System (SSDS+) supports the issuance, depository and safekeeping of tokenized debt securities, including Islamic bonds known as sukuk.

THAILAND

Bitget plans Thai crypto exchange acquisition weeks after $388M hack

Crypto exchange Bitget has announced plans to acquire Thailand’s GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics, seeking to expand its Southeast Asia footprint weeks after a major hack impacting its hot and warm wallets. 

The proposed transaction involves BTGT Management (Thailand), a company in which Bitget says it holds an interest, according to an announcement shared with Cointelegraph.  The acquisition will allow Bitget to introduce its trading platform to Thai users.

Chinese suspect in $75M international crime network arrested in Bangkok

Thai police arrested a 37-year-old Chinese man wanted by authorities in China for alleged involvement in an international crime network and money laundering.

Investigators said the network handled more than 500 million yuan ($75 million) in transactions, Thai media Khaosod English reported in a post on X on Saturday.

Police alleged the suspect was involved in cryptocurrency and foreign-currency exchanges for criminal groups across more than 133 accounts. Investigators said he attempted to evade arrest by using forged documents to report his residence and changing vehicle registration plates before police found him in a luxury house in Bangkok.

VIETNAM
Da Nang crypto sandbox targets digital tourism

The fourth largest city in Vietnan, Da Nang, is using a controlled sandbox that enables businesses to employ crypto related applications in the tourism industry. Da Nang welcomed 15.9 million visitors in the first nine months of 2026.

Vietnam-EFTA agreement includes Crypto Valley links

Vietnam has signed a free-trade agreement with the European Free Trade Association countries of Switzerland, Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein. Following a meeting with the Vietnamese PM, Swiss President Guy Parmelin proposed linking Switzerland’s Crypto Valley hub with Vietnam’s innovation ecosystem to further cooperation in blockchain, AI and quantum technology.

SINGAPORE

Singapore Gulf Bank offers retail USD-stablecoin conversion

Singapore Gulf Bank (which is actually licensed by Bahrain) announced that retail customers can convert between dollars for USDT or USDC via its mobile banking app.

Singapore-backed manager launches Swiss bitcoin ETF

The Singapore backed BIT Asset Management has launched Switzerland’s first Bitcoin ETF. Formerly known as Matrixport, it’s Zurich arm has been approved by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority to launch the country’s first spot Bitcoin ETF and Europe’s only spot Bitcoin ETF.

title: Senate's top Democratic investigator looking into Tether payments to Bo Hines' firm
summary: Senator Richard Blumenthal, the ranking Democrat on the investigations subcommittee, added a probe of the ex-White House crypto adviser to his list of crypto interests.
content:
Updated Oct 22, 2026, 7:36 p.m. EDTPublished Oct 22, 2026, 6:43 p.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal keeps digging into Tether on behalf of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, this time looking at recent reports that a firm owned by former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines took millions while he was still helping shape stablecoin policy.
  • Blumenthal, the ranking Democrat on the subcommittee, sent letters to Tether and the firm, Nxum, that was co-founded by Hines, who took a job as Tether’s top U.S. executive after leaving the White House.

U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal has added another Tether probe to the many irons he has in crypto fires, this time demanding answers about reported payments the company made to a firm owned by Bo Hines — the former White House crypto adviser who is now in charge of the U.S. arm of Tether.

Blumenthal, the ranking Democrat on the Senate's Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, sent letters Thursday to Tether and to the consulting company Hines started with his father and another partner, Nxum Group.

"The highly unusual terms and nature of Tether’s business relationship with both Nxum and Bo Hines raise alarming ethical and legal concerns, indicating that Tether was likely well aware of the illegality and impropriety of issuing payments to a current White House official with such a direct role in shaping cryptocurrency legislation that was instrumental to its business," Blumenthal wrote to Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino.

The Wall Street Journal reported last week that Nxum had received large payments for consulting work for Tether when Hines was still advising President Donald Trump and his administration on crypto policy (including on stablecoin issuers significant to Tether). Blumenthal requested details of those business arrangements.

“Tether is aware of the allegations reported in The Wall Street Journal that form the basis of Senator Blumenthal’s letter,” the company said in a statement. “External counsel previously conducted an in-depth internal investigation into the matter, which found no evidence of wrongdoing.”

CoinDesk had been first to report earlier that Hines' company — which had little track record or experience in politics — was making millions of dollars as the main campaign-advertising provider for a political action committee associated with Tether.

Hines' family firm, Nxum, has recently hired another official that worked as a White House crypto adviser, Harry Jung. The office that advised Trump on crypto issues has since gone vacant, with the departure of Patrick Witt, who had replaced Hines as its executive director.

Blumenthal has been focusing significant attention on crypto, including on Trump's memecoin, crypto backers of the president's projects, Trump family crypto firm World Liberty Financial, activities at Binance and especially on Tether. He issued a report on its financial connections to Iran, and he more recently demanded answers about Tether's connection to its U.S. financial partner, Cantor Fitzgerald.

Tether's Ardoino criticized the senator's work this week, saying Blumenthal ignored important information and shared his report with the press before giving the company a look or a chance to respond.

Though Blumenthal's party has been in the Senate minority during Trump's time in office, the still-narrow odds of Democrats taking back that chamber have improved in recent weeks. If Blumenthal returns to chair the investigations subcommittee, it would grant him significantly greater powers to subpoena and control the agenda, and he's made it clear that crypto would be high on his list of topic areas. Prediction market Kalshi gives Democrats a 69% chance at the moment.

title: Experts Warn of Systemic Risks as Crypto Lending Vaults Cross $10B
summary: Total deposits in crypto lending vaults have expanded from $4 billion in early 2025 to over $10 billion, driven by institutional investors and treasuries seeking high yield on stablecoins. Industry experts advocate for stricter risk management and financial compensation buffers for security breaches...
content:
Total deposits in crypto lending vaults have expanded from $4 billion in early 2025 to over $10 billion, driven by institutional investors and treasuries seeking high yield on stablecoins. Industry experts advocate for stricter risk management and financial compensation buffers for security breaches or negligence.

Key Takeaways

  • DeFi lending deposits surged past $10 billion from $4 billion in early 2025, driven by institutional investors.
  • Experts warn that collateral reuse and liquidity mismatches across platforms could trigger systemic contagion.
  • Echo Base and Zigfinance executives advocate for stricter risk management and Basel III-style capital buffers.

Crypto Lending Vaults Surpass $10B

Deposits in decentralized finance (DeFi) crypto lending vaults have crossed $10 billion, marking a sharp increase from approximately $4 billion at the start of 2025, according to a recent Financial Times report. The surge is driven by investors seeking higher yields on stablecoins and other tokens rather than leaving capital idle.

While highlighting the innovation, efficiency, and growing institutional adoption of DeFi smart-contract vaults compared to the opaque centralized lenders of 2022, the report frames the expansion as a “regulatory blind spot.” It warns that investors chasing double-digit yields are frequently unaware of underlying systemic, smart-contract, and illiquidity risks.

Although the report stops short of calling for immediate government intervention, it places the sector directly in the crosshairs of global regulators. Industry experts argue the moment should serve as a wake-up call, urging platforms to address risk controls proactively before a major failure triggers a regulatory crackdown.

Systemic Vulnerabilities and Exposure

Some analysts, including the anonymous owner of the crypto casino platform 1win, contend the core challenge is not the volume of capital entering crypto lending, but whether platforms can withstand severe market stress.

Abdul Rafay Gadit, co-founder and chief commercial officer at Zigfinance, acknowledged that while platforms are taking steps to implement risk-management frameworks, adoption remains uneven.

“In parts of the market, growth is running ahead of safeguards, particularly around underwriting and liquidity,” Gadit told Bitcoin.com News. “Liquidations, oracles, and isolated markets are useful controls, but their effectiveness still depends on accurate pricing, sound collateral, and available buyers when markets are stressed.”

Gadit cautioned that current fee structures often exacerbate these risks by rewarding asset growth and high yields without enforcing accountability for potential losses. When asked how a major failure or liquidation cascade could impact the broader market, he cited collateral reuse as the primary vulnerability.

“A vault share can be borrowed against elsewhere, creating another layer of leverage on the same underlying assets,” Gadit explained. “If its value or liquidity collapses, liquidations can spread across connected markets. Different platforms can end up carrying the same economic exposure.”

He also highlighted liquidity mismatch as a secondary threat, noting that vaults offering rapid withdrawals against private loans or locked positions risk depleting liquid reserves during sudden exit waves—leaving remaining investors holding illiquid assets.

“An exchange distributing the product can then face a trust crisis even without taking the credit loss itself,” Gadit said. “The question is how much common exposure sits behind products that appear diversified.”

Setting Standards and the Regulatory Debate

As official scrutiny intensifies, industry analysts broadly agree that platforms must institute rigorous standards for collateral management, disclosure, and liquidity.

To mitigate cascading liquidations, experts recommend establishing published eligibility criteria, conservative haircuts, and strict limits on circular or related-party collateral. Beyond basic proof-of-reserves audits, analysts advocate for “proof of exposure”—demanding clear disclosure of where capital is deployed, the degree of leverage involved, and independent verification of off-chain counterparty risks.

Redemption terms must also align with underlying asset lockups, supported by curator capital at risk and insurance-style safeguards to protect users against exploits or negligence.

However, debate remains over whether self-regulation can adequately protect market participants as institutional adoption scales. Analysts suggest that smart contracts alone cannot eliminate market shocks, warning that proportional oversight and independent scrutiny of underwriting will become unavoidable—particularly as certain vault architectures risk falling under existing securities laws.

The Case for Risk-Based Capital

Highlighting the structural fragility of the current ecosystem, August Widmer, partner in investments at Echo Base, argued that the absence of mandatory capital buffers leaves the sector uniquely vulnerable.

“Regulation tends to lag innovation, and unfortunately that gap is often where the consumer is left exposed,” Widmer said. “While depository institutions are subject to Basel III capital requirements, most crypto companies have no such guardrails—they can extend endless amounts of risk with no mandatory capital buffer. The result is an industry of large conglomerates at high risk of total failure yet managing customer assets across numerous business verticals.”

Widmer noted that in an interconnected digital asset environment, an unhedged failure at a single protocol often causes widespread contagion, referencing the early 2026 Kelp DAO exploit that threatened major DeFi lending protocols.

“In the interdependent world of crypto, failure at one institution often leads to failure at another,” Widmer explained. “When one leg of the crypto stool breaks, the entire stool collapses.”

To prevent systemic failures, Widmer suggested adapting established financial frameworks to digital asset markets, even if doing so tempers rapid expansion.

“Implementing a framework similar to Basel III, yet tailored to the industry, would inevitably add cost and slow development, but would almost certainly create a safer, more stable environment,” Widmer said. “The crypto industry needs to ask itself if the tradeoff is worth it. Is operating like a high-growth Jenga tower worth the failures and customer losses?”

title: Bitcoin Flashes Bull Market Signal Amid Fresh ETF Inflows: Cryptoquant CEO
summary: Bitcoin’s latest capital-flow signal resembles patterns seen during earlier bull markets, Cryptoquant CEO Ki Young Ju said. His assessment coincides with approximately $1.07 billion in U.S. spot bitcoin fund inflows over three sessions through Oct. 21, adding a separate sign of renewed demand. Fresh...
content:
Bitcoin’s latest capital-flow signal resembles patterns seen during earlier bull markets, Cryptoquant CEO Ki Young Ju said. His assessment coincides with approximately $1.07 billion in U.S. spot bitcoin fund inflows over three sessions through Oct. 21, adding a separate sign of renewed demand.

Key Takeaways

  • Fresh capital points to a bitcoin bull market, Ki Young Ju argues.
  • His chart links renewed capital growth with patterns from earlier rallies.
  • The underlying metric values coins at their last blockchain movement price.

Fresh Capital Points to Bull Market Conditions

Bitcoin is attracting fresh capital in a pattern associated with bull markets, Cryptoquant founder and CEO Ki Young Ju stated on Oct. 21. In his comment on bitcoin capital inflows shared on X, the head of the blockchain analytics company presented a realized-capitalization chart comparing the metric with bitcoin’s price across multiple market cycles.

Ju stated:

“Fresh capital is flowing into bitcoin. This only happens in bull markets.”

The accompanying chart distinguishes periods of rising realized capitalization in green from intervals when the measure was flat or declining in gray. Earlier green stretches appear around the 2017 rally, the 2020-2021 expansion, and the subsequent advance into 2025. Its latest segment also turns green, supporting his interpretation of renewed inflows.

How Bitcoin’s Capital Signal Is Calculated

Realized capitalization estimates bitcoin’s aggregate cost basis by valuing each coin at the price when it last moved on the blockchain. The realized-cap calculation differs from market capitalization, which values every coin at the current market price.

Each transaction spends existing outputs and creates new ones, establishing the blockchain records used in this calculation. As bitcoin transaction inputs and outputs change, transferred coins acquire updated valuations. Rising realized cap is commonly interpreted as fresh investment, although transfers between a holder’s own wallets can also affect the measure.

Holder profitability provides another perspective on market cycles, alongside the capital movements highlighted in Ju’s latest assessment. Cryptoquant’s profitability-based bitcoin cycle indicators featured in a July 14 analysis suggesting the cycle’s peak could still lie ahead. That assessment examined valuation ratios and investor profits through a separate framework.

ETF Flows Add Context to Bitcoin’s Bull Market Signal

U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) attracted approximately $524.8 million on Oct. 21, extending their inflow streak to three sessions. Those three-day bitcoin ETF inflows totaled approximately $1.07 billion. Blackrock’s IBIT led the day’s additions with $235 million, followed by Fidelity’s FBTC with $212.7 million. Grayscale’s GBTC attracted $32.6 million, while Bitwise’s BITB recorded $19.2 million in inflows.

Bitcoin was trading near $81,000 on Oct. 22 after retreating from an Oct. 21 intraday high near $84,739. Approximately $35.5 billion in bitcoin changed hands over the preceding 24 hours.

title: Birdeye Launches Peak Terminal For Institutional Crypto Research
summary: Birdeye has launched Peak, a subscription terminal combining digital-asset market data, fundamentals and portfolio analytics. Its pitch centers on consistent data across venues, rather than another isolated trading dashboard.
content:
TL;DR: Birdeye has launched Peak, a subscription terminal combining digital-asset market data, fundamentals and portfolio analytics. Its pitch centers on consistent data across venues, rather than another isolated trading dashboard.

Institutional crypto researchers have another terminal to evaluate. Birdeye launched Peak on Wednesday, bringing several of its data and analysis services into one professional workspace.

The company’s October 21 announcement describes coverage spanning centralized and decentralized venues, with ETF flows, filings and private-funding information alongside on-chain data. Access is sold by seat and organization.

The official product page lists token supply and unlock information, holder concentration, wallet-level portfolio analysis, protocol metrics and institutional indices. A command-based interface lets users move between different objects and views, while a research layer called Peak AI is intended to surface connections across datasets.

The Value Depends On Consistent Definitions

Putting several data feeds into one screen can save time. It does not automatically make the figures comparable.

For a researcher examining an asset, circulating supply, fully diluted valuation and an upcoming unlock each describe something different. A wallet transfer might be a sale, a custody move or an internal reorganization. A large volume figure can also look more useful than it is if the methodology does not distinguish between types of activity.

Those are the practical problems an institutional terminal must solve if it is to support decisions beyond simple price monitoring. Users need to trace a number to its source and understand the assumptions behind it.

Birdeye says owning its on-chain indexing infrastructure lets it reconcile records and apply consistent definitions. That is the company’s explanation of its approach, rather than an independent audit of every metric delivered by Peak.

The product has not been performance-tested for this article, and the launch release does not establish that an AI-generated connection between datasets is a verified investment conclusion.

For prospective users, the relevant test will be whether the terminal makes research reproducible: can a colleague reach the same result, identify the same inputs and explain why the number changed? Peak’s launch puts that question in front of institutional desks with a new product built around it.

title: Circle shareholder sues Trump, World Liberty and Steve Witkoff over crypto deals
summary: According to a Circle shareholder, the US president’s “corruption” through USD1 left the company unable to compete with stablecoins, harming USDC.
content:
Update (Oct. 22, 10:27 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include a statement from the White House.

A shareholder for Circle Internet Financial, the company behind the USDC (USDC) stablecoin, filed a lawsuit against US President Donald Trump, his family’s crypto company World Liberty Financial, affiliate entities, and US Special Envoy to the Middle East Steve Witkoff over a $2 billion deal between a foreign government entity and Binance.

In a Thursday filing in the US District Court for the District of Columbia, Circle shareholder J. Benjamin Greenberg alleged that Trump, Witkoff and World Liberty caused harm to Circle by creating a pathway for foreign governments to funnel money using the Trump family crypto company’s USD1 stablecoin. This “brazen corruption,” according to Greenberg, leaves Circle “unable to compete” in the stablecoin market with its USDC.

Central to the Circle shareholder’s allegations is an Abu Dhabi entity, MGX, tied to the United Arab Emirates royalty, which invested $2 billion into cryptocurrency exchange Binance using the USD1 stablecoin in 2025. The Wall Street Journal reported in February that another investment vehicle backed by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan agreed to purchase a 49% stake in World Liberty for $500 million.

“By accepting hundreds of millions of dollars from a foreign government, the President and his companies have diverted business from [Circle],” alleged Greenberg, adding:

“Plaintiff asks this Court to declare the President’s corrupt acts a violation of the Constitution, to enjoin the brazen corruption alleged below, to order an accounting of the billions in payments from foreign states to the President and his businesses, to require the companies holding them to disgorge the emoluments the President accepted through them, and for compensatory and punitive damages.”

Related: Trump didn‘t mention ‘crypto’ once in White House cybercrime roundtable

Greenberg reported holding 10,000 ordinary shares of Circle as part of his reasons for the lawsuit. He petitioned the court to declare that Trump violated the US Constitution’s Foreign Emoluments Clause through the crypto deals and to issue injunctions preventing the president and Witkoff from pursuing similar financial interests without Congress’ consent.

Zach Witkoff, the son of the Witkoff named in the lawsuit, is a World Liberty co-founder. Trump and his three sons are also co-founders of the crypto venture.

A Circle spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the company “did not initiate, direct, authorize, or participate in the filing,” declining to comment on pending litigation. White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said that Trump had “no conflicts of interest“ with his crypto investments, calling the lawsuit “frivolous.“ A spokesperson for World Liberty did not respond to a request for comment on the lawsuit.

Democrats use ’corruption’ messaging as midterm elections approach

The US president and his family are tied to several crypto ventures that Trump reported netted him $1.4 billion in 2025, while also costing investors about $4.7 billion, according to reporting by the nonprofit consumer advocacy organization Public Citizen. The crypto ventures are just a few of many controversial deals Trump faces scrutiny over, including accepting a jet from the government of Qatar.

With less than two weeks until the 2026 midterms and early voting having already started in some US states, Democrats running for reelection are using Trump’s crypto deals as a wedge issue for voters to support candidates in their party. Last week, Senator Mark Warner released a campaign ad highlighting that the president made ”more than $600 million alone from the crypto memecoin.”

title: Circle Shareholder Sues Trump, Alleging Unconstitutional Profits From $2B UAE Crypto Deals
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Circle Shareholder Sues Trump, Alleging Unconstitutional Profits From $2B UAE Crypto Deals
A shareholder of stablecoin giant Circle has alleged the president corruptly cashed in on crypto deals. 
This post Circle Shareholder Sues Trump, Alleging Unconstitutional Profits From $2B UA...
content:
A shareholder from one of the world’s biggest digital asset companies has sued U.S. President Donald Trump for alleged crypto corruption. 

The lawsuit, filed on Thursday by shareholder and former Circle employee J. Benjamin Greenberg, alleges that a member of the United Arab Emirates ruling family agreed to pay half a billion dollars into the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial business — in direct violation of the Constitution. 

Circle is the fintech company behind the stablecoin, USDC. Regulators in the U.S. are fast pushing ahead with pro-crypto rules despite lawmakers last month blocking landmark digital asset legislation, which President Trump backed. 

A number of lawmakers didn’t back the draft legislation — the Clarity Act — because they said that the Trump family had illicitly cashed in on crypto ventures. 

“The corruption at issue is not subtle, and it is not hidden,” the lawsuit alleges. “Since returning to office,  President Donald J. Trump and his family have built a cryptocurrency business and invited foreign states to route money to him by paying into it. Foreign money has answered.”

The lawsuit goes on to allege that an investment fund created by the government of Abu Dhabi also gave the president $2 billion via World Liberty Financial’s USD1 stablecoin product. 

World Liberty Financial is a decentralized finance project co-founded by the president and his sons.

President Trump stopped being involved in the project after taking office in 2025. 

Thursday’s lawsuit adds that the president allegedly gave the Emirati leadership access to advanced artificial intelligence chips and pardoned a convicted felon in turn for the crypto investment. It references a February Wall Street Journal article that reported the deal. 

“Although the President has dressed his corrupt arrangements in the language of new technology — tokens and stablecoins, holding companies and reserve yields — that vocabulary must not obscure what this is: the oldest form of public corruption, a public official taking money from a foreign power,” the lawsuit further says. 

It alleges that the president has “corruptly” profited from $2 billion via the deals. 

President Trump, World Liberty, and U.S. Middle East Special Envoy Steve Witkoff are named as the defendants in the lawsuit. 

The president campaigned on a ticket to help the crypto industry and received major financial backing from the space but some Washington lawmakers have criticized the way the Trump family has profited from digital asset ventures.

Trump and the White House have always denied any conflicts of interest. The president in August, ahead of the crypto Clarity Act vote, said that Democrats criticizing his family crypto ventures had made money from stock trading. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Ripple Teams With Arf to Bring RLUSD Lending to XRP Ledger
summary: Ripple and Arf are bringing RLUSD, Ripple’s dollar-pegged stablecoin, to settlement financing on the XRP Ledger. The partnership targets licensed payment companies awaiting cross-border settlements, with plans to adopt lending infrastructure built directly into the network. Payment Companies Gain An...
content:
Ripple and Arf are bringing RLUSD, Ripple’s dollar-pegged stablecoin, to settlement financing on the XRP Ledger. The partnership targets licensed payment companies awaiting cross-border settlements, with plans to adopt lending infrastructure built directly into the network.

Key Takeaways

  • Arf reports approximately $10 billion in annual global settlements.
  • Its short-term financing is typically repaid within one to five days.
  • Expansion into native lending requires approval of network rule changes.

Payment Companies Gain Another Source of Settlement Funding

Licensed payment companies will gain access to RLUSD financing on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) through a partnership Arf announced on Oct. 22. The Zug, Switzerland-based settlement liquidity provider reports approximately $10 billion in annual global settlement volume. Its settlement financing partnership with Ripple will initially provide working capital directly on the network.

Arf co-founder and CEO Ali Erhat Nalbant said:

“Payment companies need capital to keep money moving while they wait for funds to settle.”

Ripple also highlighted RLUSD working capital for licensed payment companies in an Oct. 22 post on X. Participating financial institutions can manage fiat and stablecoin treasuries through Arf, supported by its bank accounts in major financial hubs. The underlying blockchain operates behind the scenes.

Repayments typically arrive within one to five days as the underlying payments settle, according to Arf’s announcement. That allows funds to be lent again across successive transactions. The company reports that its capital turns over four times monthly across its existing business.

Native XRPL Lending Depends on Network Approval

Arf plans to move more of its financing activity onto XRPL’s native lending infrastructure once it becomes available. Single Asset Vaults would pool and manage funds on the blockchain, while the Lending Protocol would enable loans from those pools. Arf would retain responsibility for credit assessments and working capital decisions outside the network.

XRPL documentation describes fixed-term lending from pooled assets and mechanisms for recording loan terms and managing repayments. These functions would administer financing after the lender and borrower agree on terms, with loan activity recorded directly on the ledger.

The institutional credit framework outlined by Ripple in June identifies two technical specifications: XLS-65 defines Single Asset Vaults, while XLS-66 specifies the Lending Protocol. These describe how pooled capital would be held and extended as loans.

XLS-65 and XLS-66 are amendments, changes to network rules that require validator approval before taking effect on mainnet, XRPL’s live transaction network. Current requirements also include LendingProtocolV1_1, an amendment updating vault and lending rules.

RLUSD Financing Builds on Institutional Lending Plans

RLUSD would serve as the asset for loan disbursements and repayments, extending the use of dollar-linked stablecoins in payment settlement. XRP would support network operations through transaction fees and reserve requirements for accounts and certain ledger objects, giving the two assets distinct functions within the arrangement.

Soil, a fintech lending platform operated by institutional asset manager Orqo Group, is also preparing to use the proposed infrastructure. Its institutional vault plans center on pooling RLUSD from institutional lenders, with blockchain records supporting loan accounting and reporting.

Clearpool, a decentralized lending marketplace, and Cicada Partners, an institutional credit manager, are developing a separate RLUSD lending initiative for fintech, payments, and cryptocurrency businesses. Clearpool is building the lending infrastructure, while Cicada will select borrowers and monitor credit risk.

Arf has already developed an implementation against the proposed protocol and will continue providing feedback as a design partner. It plans to transition its program to native lending infrastructure after the required amendments activate on mainnet.

title: Google’s Updated UAE Crypto Advertising Rules Take Effect
summary: Google’s updated rules for UAE-targeted crypto exchange and wallet ads took effect October 21. Advertisers need an accepted local license and Google certification; the policy is not blanket permission for all crypto promotions.
content:
TL;DR: Google’s updated rules for UAE-targeted crypto exchange and wallet ads took effect October 21. Advertisers need an accepted local license and Google certification; the policy is not blanket permission for all crypto promotions.

Crypto exchanges and software-wallet providers targeting customers in the United Arab Emirates now face the licensing and certification conditions set out in Google’s updated advertising policy.

The change took effect on October 21, according to Google’s official policy notice. This is the implementation date of an earlier announcement, rather than a newly issued rule on Wednesday.

For the crypto exchange and software-wallet category, Google lists four accepted authorities: the Capital Market Authority, Dubai Financial Services Authority, Financial Services Regulatory Authority and Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority. Advertisers also need certification from Google.

A License And An Ad Approval Are Separate Steps

A financial-services authorization and permission to distribute an advertisement answer different questions. The first concerns the business’s regulated activities. The second concerns whether a particular platform will carry its marketing under that platform’s rules.

The updated notice links those processes but does not merge them. Possessing a license does not, on its own, establish that an advertiser has completed Google’s certification process.

Equally, a reader encountering an ad should not treat its appearance as an assurance about investment returns or a guarantee against loss. Advertising eligibility concerns access to the marketing channel; it is not an assessment of every transaction a customer might make afterward.

For firms, the operational consequences sit with campaign preparation. A company needs its authorization and certification details to match the service it is promoting and the jurisdiction it is targeting. Marketing teams cannot safely infer that eligibility in one market automatically carries over to another.

The notice also discusses other financial-product categories. Those should not be collapsed into one universal crypto rule: the license list above is the one Google provides specifically for cryptocurrency exchanges and software wallets targeting the UAE.

The immediate change is therefore precise. Eligible providers have an updated route to advertising access, with a local licensing requirement and a separate platform certification requirement attached.

title: Dune launches real-time data feeds covering 200 onchain trading venues
summary: The new service aims to bring onchain trading data into institutional financial systems as tokenized stock markets expand and face growing scrutiny.
content:
Blockchain analytics platform Dune has launched real-time market data feeds covering more than 200 onchain trading venues, aiming to bring decentralized market activity into the trading systems used by traditional financial institutions.

The new service provides trade data from 12 blockchains, including Ethereum, Solana, Base and XLayer, roughly one second after execution, according to a Thursday announcement.

The feeds cover spot trading across decentralized exchanges, as well as perpetual futures trading on Hyperliquid and Lighter, with standardized data on prices, trade sizes and transaction details across markets.

According to Dune co-founder and CEO Fredrik Haga, quant funds, market makers, asset managers and bank trading desks are among the first clients using the service, although he declined to identify them, citing nondisclosure agreements. Dune said the firms use the data to assess liquidity, compare prices across venues and evaluate trading strategies before committing capital.

“Most institutions are watching onchain markets first, because they can’t price these assets properly without them anymore,” Haga said. He expects direct onchain trading to follow as liquidity improves and regulatory rules catch up, adding:

What still holds institutions back is how messy it is. The same stock trades on dozens of venues across different chains, and you need to know what’s trading where before you can touch it.

Related: Ondo lets institutions convert stocks directly into tokenized shares

Tokenized stock growth brings market challenges

The market for tokenized stocks has grown sharply over the past year, but fragmented liquidity and disputes over whether companies should have a say in how their shares are traded onchain have raised questions about the market’s development.

Recently, tensions surfaced around OKXICE, a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange. The venture announced plans for a tokenized stock trading platform on Oct. 4, but has since faced objections from several publicly traded companies.

So far, 16 companies, including Microsoft, Alphabet and Goldman Sachs, have filed objections to having their shares traded on the proposed platform, although they did not specify their reasons.

Beyond issuer objections, market fragmentation poses another concern. In May, Tiger Research director Ryan Yoon warned that trading the same tokenized stocks across multiple blockchain platforms could create price discrepancies, increase slippage and reduce market efficiency.

According to RWA.xyz data, the distributed value of tokenized stocks has reached $3.58 billion, up from about $627 million a year earlier, a roughly 470% increase.

title: DeFi Giant Uniswap Taps 7 Rival Liquidity Sources to Burn UNI Tokens
summary: The decentralized exchange (DEX) platform Uniswap has turned DEX competitors into potential revenue sources for its UNI token-burning mechanism. Launched Thursday, Aggregator Hooks connect seven external liquidity sources covering more than 90% of decentralized exchange activity across Ethereum, Bas...
content:
The decentralized exchange (DEX) platform Uniswap has turned DEX competitors into potential revenue sources for its UNI token-burning mechanism. Launched Thursday, Aggregator Hooks connect seven external liquidity sources covering more than 90% of decentralized exchange activity across Ethereum, Base, and Robinhood Chain. The upgrade allows Uniswap to collect protocol fees from trades routed through outside liquidity pools, contributing to UNI burns.

Key Takeaways

  • The DEX giant Uniswap launched Aggregator Hooks on Oct. 22, connecting seven external liquidity sources across three chains.
  • Uniswap v4 collects protocol fees from trades routed through competing exchanges, contributing to UNI burns.
  • Uniswap’s expansion builds on its 2025 UNIfication initiative, which included a 100 million UNI treasury burn.

Uniswap Turns Rival Exchange Liquidity Into Fuel for UNI Burns

DeFi’s top DEX protocol by volume, Uniswap, has figured out how to collect fees from trades routed through competing DEX platforms, with the proceeds contributing to UNI token burns. On Oct. 22, 2026, the protocol launched Aggregator Hooks, connecting seven external liquidity sources directly to Uniswap v4.

The integration spans Ethereum mainnet and the Layer 2 networks Base and Robinhood Chain, covering more than 90% of decentralized exchange activity across those networks. Even when another platform supplies the liquidity, Uniswap can collect protocol fees, effectively turning rival trading activity into another source of UNI burn revenue.

Uniswap Opens Its Trading Engine to Rival Exchanges

“Uniswap v4 is now an aggregator,” Uniswap Labs announced Thursday, introducing a system that makes outside liquidity appear as native v4 pools. The company explained that its exchange has processed more than $4.5 trillion in cumulative swaps, but liquidity continues forming elsewhere. “Aggregator Hooks bring it in, benefiting the protocol,” Uniswap Labs further stated.

The technology automatically compares prices across Uniswap and connected exchanges, including Curve, Fluid, Pancakeswap V3, and Slipstream. Quotes refresh every block, with trades settling in a single transaction. “The whole route settles in a single transaction, with nothing new to approve,” the company explained.

Outside Trading Volume Feeds UNI Token Burns

The financial arrangement builds on Uniswap’s UNIfication initiative, approved in December 2025, which activated protocol fees and directed collected revenue toward UNI burns. Under the mechanism, fees accumulate in TokenJar contracts, while the Firepit system requires UNI destruction before those assets can be withdrawn. The initiative also authorized a one-time treasury burn of 100 million UNI.

Uniswap Labs confirmed the connection, stating, “Outside sources become v4 pools, and swaps routed through them pay protocol fees, contributing to UNI burn.” The feature is already active through Uniswap’s Web App and API, with additional networks and liquidity sources planned.

For competing DEX protocols, the arrangement presents an interesting trade-off: More potential trading volume from Uniswap users, but protocol fees flowing toward a rival’s token-burning machinery.

title: Zcash Foundation Details Zebra Sync Fixes Ahead Of NU7 Release
summary: The Zcash Foundation says it merged fixes for Zebra nodes that stopped syncing near the chain tip. The October 21 update places the work ahead of a stable NU7 release and reminds operators of the older client’s approaching stop date.
content:
TL;DR: The Zcash Foundation says it merged fixes for Zebra nodes that stopped syncing near the chain tip. The October 21 update places the work ahead of a stable NU7 release and reminds operators of the older client’s approaching stop date.

Zcash’s preparation for NU7 includes a less glamorous but essential task: making sure nodes keep following the chain reliably.

In an engineering update published Wednesday, the Zcash Foundation described fixes for synchronization problems reported after Zebra 7.0.0-rc.0. Its team also confirmed the same underlying cause on a mainnet node.

The changes adjust how Zebra requests blocks from peers and handles failed downloads. At the time of the update, the work was merged into the development branch but had not appeared in a published release. The foundation described Zebra 7.0.0 as the likely next stable NU7 release.

Merged Code Still Has To Reach Operators

That release distinction matters. A fix being accepted into development does not mean an exchange, wallet provider or individual node is already running it.

Operators normally receive the benefit when an appropriate release is published and deployed. Services relying on their own nodes then need to establish that those nodes have caught up and continue to follow the network correctly.

The update also describes improvements to handling ZEC amounts through Zebra’s RPC types and a migration guide for services moving from zcashd’s interface. These are integration concerns that can affect the reliability of downstream systems even when they do not change what an ordinary transaction looks like.

An Approaching Operational Deadline

The foundation repeated that Zebra 6.4.x is designed to stop around November 2, making an upgrade to the NU7 release an operational requirement for affected mainnet users. The broader NU7 planning thread provides the surrounding upgrade schedule.

The October 21 report covers engineering work from October 6–19. It should be read as a dated account of readiness, not as proof that every item was already deployed across the network or that every subsequent release decision had been completed.

There is also no basis in this update for describing the synchronization issue as a theft of coins. The reported problem concerns node behavior and the work needed to deliver a stable client ahead of the upgrade.

title: Spout Finance – Let Your Stocks Pay the Interest
summary: Marc Ryan is Co-Founder and CEO of Spout Finance, a Solana lending protocol that lets people borrow USDC against tokenized US stocks without paying interest. Based in New York, Marc first got into crypto during the 2017 ICO boom and stayed through DeFi summer and the NFT cycle. Meanwhile he worked a...
content:
Skip to content

Marc Ryan is Co-Founder and CEO of Spout Finance, a Solana lending protocol that lets people borrow USDC against tokenized US stocks without paying interest. Based in New York, Marc first got into crypto during the 2017 ICO boom and stayed through DeFi summer and the NFT cycle. Meanwhile he worked as a technology investment banker at HSBC, covering fintech, software and hardware, and that experience showed him how cheaply wealthy clients could borrow against their portfolios compared with everyone else.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

Spout starts from an argument about who tokenized stocks are really for. Marc points out that anyone with meaningful capital, almost anywhere in the world, can already open an Interactive Brokers account and buy US equities, so putting shares on a blockchain is not much of a breakthrough by itself. The more interesting question is what onchain stocks can do that brokerage stocks can’t. His answer is a lending pool that works like Aave or Kamino, with one structural difference. Instead of charging borrowers interest, Spout sells covered calls on their collateral every week, set well above the current price, and uses the premiums to pay lenders. Borrowers can take out up to half the value of their tokenized shares in USDC. The cost shows up as a small cap on their upside, which Marc estimates averages under half a percent a year, compared with margin rates of roughly 4.5% at the cheap end and 20% or more at some emerging-market brokers. Lenders, meanwhile, earn premium income that doesn’t depend on whether the stock goes up or down.

The conversation also covers how a small startup positions itself in a sector that is now attracting major institutions. Marc says most of the investors in Spout’s recent $2 million round were chosen for what they bring beyond money. Anchorage Digital provides the institutional custody that large funds require, Solana is the chain he considers best suited for bringing retail onto financial assets, and former CFTC Chairman Chris Giancarlo advises on navigating US regulation. Marc also explains why Spout gave up issuing its own tokenized shares. Running issuance alongside a lending protocol created too much legal and corporate overhead, so the team chose to be a permissionless layer that works with every issuer instead of competing with them. Most of those issuers wrap shares held with a custodian such as Alpaca. Marc contrasts that with native issuance from firms like Securitize and Superstate, where the shares themselves live onchain and can be self-custodied.

That distinction frames his view of the current regulatory fight. After a batch of companies objected to having their shares tokenized on OKXICE, the joint venture between OKX and NYSE owner ICE, under the SEC’s new Innovation Exemption, Marc argues that wrappers will keep serving offshore investors. US access, in his view, will come through native issuance or closer work with the DTCC. He is candid that a Spout token is undecided. If one launches, it would boost lender rates and allow options to be sold further out of the money. In the hot take round, Marc places himself between Bitcoin maximalism and multi-chain opportunism. He says every public equity will eventually move onchain, describes how AI agents now run parts of his own business, and names Back to the Future as his favorite film.
