title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, Bitcoin mining competition intensified as network hashrate reached a seven-month high despite the industry’s shift toward AI. Separately, Starknet voters backed research into becoming an independent layer-1 blockchain, and the PHP Foundation acknowledged delays in fixing a critical security flaw that prompted government websites to go offline.

Bitcoin mining competition heats up despite AI exodus

Bitcoin’s network hashrate has reached a seven-month high despite major mining companies shifting their computing capacity toward AI, signaling growing competition in the space, according to BlocksBridge Consulting.

Bitcoin’s seven-day average hashrate has climbed above 1 zettahash per second for the first time since March 3, suggesting that computing power leaving the network is being replaced by other miners.

Hashrate measures the computing power securing Bitcoin’s network, while mining difficulty determines how hard it is to earn new Bitcoin.

Mining difficulty increased 5.92% on Oct. 16, with BlocksBridge projecting another 5.16% increase at the next adjustment. Combined, that would represent an 11.4% increase across two adjustments, making it harder for miners to earn rewards.

The increase comes despite publicly traded mining companies reporting a 23% decline in realized hashrate as they redirect resources toward AI. Their AI-related revenue increased 52% quarter over quarter.

BlocksBridge estimates that roughly $1.5 billion worth of mining equipment has been displaced by the transition.

Some of that hardware may be finding new buyers among smaller miners with access to cheaper electricity, allowing them to expand operations while larger competitors pursue AI.

Starknet voters back research into life beyond Ethereum

Starknet’s community has voted to support research into becoming an independent, post-quantum layer-1 blockchain.

The network’s potential departure from Ethereum gained overwhelming support. The governance vote that ran for seven days closed on Thursday. The poll drew about 3,200 votes, with 93.52% of voting power in favor of the transition.

The non-binding poll recorded the highest participation in Starknet’s governance history, according to StarkWare, which said it abstained from voting to leave the decision to the community.

The outcome allows StarkWare and the Starknet Foundation to proceed with research into an independent L1. The actual shift itself would require a separate, binding governance vote. For now, Starknet will continue operating as an Ethereum layer-2 network. 

“We’re beginning work on a whitepaper even before we start the weekend, and hope to release a draft for public scrutiny in November,” StarkWare CEO Eli Ben-Sasson told Cointelegraph. 

PHP Foundation admits ‘structural failure’ delayed critical security fix

The PHP Foundation has acknowledged that indecision and a shortage of resources delayed a fix for a critical security flaw first identified in 2024, calling the stalled response a “structural failure.” 

Government agencies and other organizations worldwide took websites offline Wednesday as a precaution while PHP released emergency patches for two related critical vulnerabilities. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers without logging in. 

PHP is a programming language widely used to power websites and web applications, including content management systems. 

In a blog post following the release of the patch, the foundation described how its developers first found signs of the vulnerability in 2024, but struggled to come up with a solution without disrupting the large ecosystem of software built using PHP.

“Combined with the lack of a known path to remote code execution and the small team of core developers with the necessary deep knowledge of the engine occupied with many responsibilities, this decision process caused work on a fix to stall and restart repeatedly over months,” said the foundation.

“We won’t pretend otherwise: the delay was a structural failure, caused by both the security team’s decision process and its lack of resources.”

The foundation was pointed to the vulnerability again on August 11, after security firm Calif and OpenAI independently reported the same underlying issue, with Calif demonstrating unconditional remote code execution, which made it a top security priority.

title: Starknet Moves Toward Post-Quantum Layer 1 as Voters Back Ethereum Split
summary: Starknet is taking its first formal steps toward potentially becoming an independent, quantum-resistant Layer 1 blockchain, following a community vote that overwhelmingly supported researching a departure from its current role as an Ethereum Layer 2 network. STRK Holders Approve Layer 1 Exploration ...
content:
Starknet is taking its first formal steps toward potentially becoming an independent, quantum-resistant Layer 1 blockchain, following a community vote that overwhelmingly supported researching a departure from its current role as an Ethereum Layer 2 network.

Key Takeaways

  • Starknet community backs Layer 1 exploration: 93.52% voted to research transitioning from an Ethereum Layer 2 to a standalone blockchain.
  • Starknet aims to eliminate Ethereum dependencies and strengthen its resistance to future quantum threats.
  • StarkWare will study technical challenges, while CEO Eli Ben-Sasson touts Starknet’s security, privacy, and scalability advantages.

STRK Holders Approve Layer 1 Exploration

The Starknet Foundation announced Thursday that 93.52% of voting power supported exploring the transition in a non-binding governance poll that concluded Oct. 22. The result gives StarkWare and the Starknet Foundation a mandate to investigate the technical requirements, trade-offs, and potential consequences of operating Starknet as a standalone blockchain.

The vote does not authorize an immediate transition. Instead, a joint working group will begin research and publish its findings before any formal proposals are submitted for additional community votes. No implementation timeline has been established.

The proposal reflects growing concerns about the long-term security of blockchain networks as quantum computing advances threaten the cryptographic systems underpinning many cryptocurrencies.

Starknet currently relies on Ethereum for settlement and data availability, creating dependencies that could complicate its efforts to achieve comprehensive post-quantum security. While Starknet’s underlying zero-knowledge technology is designed to resist quantum attacks, components tied to Ethereum remain dependent on that network’s upgrade schedule.

StarkWare first floated the idea of an independent Layer 1 network on Oct. 8, arguing that Starknet could gain greater control over its security by reducing those dependencies.

StarkWare CEO Eli Ben-Sasson welcomed the vote, presenting the potential transition as part of a broader effort to make Starknet adaptable to future technological challenges.

“Starknet has everything it needs to evolve and improve, be it for post-quantum security, better UX, scale, privacy, or any other desired trait,” Ben-Sasson wrote on X following the vote.

He pointed to Starknet’s cryptographic architecture as a key advantage. Its zero-knowledge scalable transparent arguments of knowledge, or ZK-STARKs, rely on hash-based cryptography designed with quantum resistance in mind. Starknet’s programmable accounts can also adopt new signature schemes without requiring a protocol upgrade.

However, Ben-Sasson acknowledged that further work would be necessary to make the entire network resistant to quantum threats.

Beyond security, Ben-Sasson highlighted privacy and user experience as important components of Starknet’s long-term strategy. He specifically pointed to STRK20, a privacy framework designed to support confidential decentralized finance activities while preserving the composability and usability of blockchain applications.

The privacy push has already produced new tools. Earlier this month, StarkWare introduced Shadow Accounts, which allow users to interact with decentralized applications through pseudonymous identities without publicly linking those activities to their primary wallets.

STRK Sinks After Successful Vote

Under the proposed Layer 1 approach, STRK would remain Starknet’s native token, with no plans to introduce a replacement. Bridges between Ethereum and Starknet would also remain operational, preserving connections between the ecosystems.

The price of STRK tumbled on Thursday following the vote, recently down about 14% in the past 24 hours at a price near $0.054. That’s pushed the asset’s price decline to 40% over the last week alone, following a spike above $0.12 on Oct. 11. The token is down nearly 99% since peaking at $4.41 in Feb. 2024.

The next stage will focus on determining whether an independent network can deliver the promised security benefits without introducing unacceptable technical or economic trade-offs.

For Starknet, the stakes extend beyond preparing for quantum computers. A successful transition would represent a fundamental change in its relationship with Ethereum, potentially transforming one of the network’s prominent scaling solutions into a competing base-layer blockchain.

title: Blockchain Association Presses Congress on Crypto Taxes as Clarity Act Stalls
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Blockchain Association Presses Congress on Crypto Taxes as Clarity Act Stalls
The Blockchain Association asked congressional leaders Thursday to pass bipartisan crypto tax legislation, but with the Clarity Act near dead, the House bill stripped of mining and staking relief, and Con...
content:
The Blockchain Association sent a letter to Senate and House leadership on Thursday asking Congress to pass bipartisan digital asset tax legislation, the group’s first broad push on taxes since the Clarity Act failed in the Senate last month.

The letter, signed by Chief Policy Officer Lindsay Fraser and addressed to Majority Leader John Thune, Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, Speaker Mike Johnson and Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, argues that the rules governing the 67 million Americans who hold digital assets “were written for a different era.” 

The group paired it with a new site, TaxClarityforAmerica.com, built for constituents to contact their representatives.

The asks will sound familiar to anyone who has followed the tax fight: a de minimis exemption for small transactions, cash treatment for stablecoins, tax on mining and staking rewards at sale instead of receipt, broker reporting limited to firms that hold customer assets, and wash sale rules that close loss harvesting without catching everyday transactions. 

The letter adds a safe harbor for foreign traders on U.S. exchanges, a mark-to-market election, and R&D credit eligibility for blockchain development. What the letter leaves out is an endorsement. Two bills are somewhat in play, and the association named neither.

Where the tax bills stand

The House moved first. One day after the Clarity Act failed in the Senate, the Ways and Means Committee approved the Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act, H.R. 10357, a 114-page package from Chairman Jason Smith (R-MO). It exempts network fees under $10 from capital gains reporting, with a carve-out for taxpayers who made more than 5,000 transfers in the prior year, and extends wash sale and constructive sale rules to digital assets. Qualified dollar stablecoins are exempt from the wash sale rule.

The package left out the provision the industry wanted most. Rep. Mike Carey’s Tax Clarity for Mining and Staking Act, H.R. 9175, which would have let miners and stakers defer tax until they sell, was in an early discussion draft and gone from the text the committee released on September 14. Instead the bill classifies validation rewards as ordinary income, taxable on receipt. Rep. Steven Horsford (D-NV), who had proposed capping the deferral at five years, voted for the package and said it leaves the question open for further work.

The Blockchain Association, Crypto Council for Innovation and Digital Chamber had asked the committee in June to pass that bill without changes. The committee did the opposite.

The Senate has its own version. Sen. Steve Daines (R-MT) introduced the ADAPT Act on September 30 with Sens. Cynthia Lummis, Bernie Moreno and Tim Scott as cosponsors. It exempts purchases made with GENIUS Act stablecoins from gain or loss, sets the same $10 fee threshold, and applies wash sale rules with grandfathering for existing holdings and exemptions for mining and staking rewards. It sits in committee. 

Lummis’s earlier bill, S. 2207, with a $300 per-transaction de minimis exemption capped at $5,000 a year, has been in the Finance Committee since June 2025.

Neither chamber’s bill contains the exemption for small bitcoin purchases that the industry made a centerpiece at Bitcoin 2026. The House bill’s $10 threshold covers fees, not purchases. The Senate bill’s spending exemption covers stablecoins, not bitcoin. 

The Bitcoin Policy Institute and others have argued that any de minimis rule should cover bitcoin, and Thursday’s letter asks for a “meaningful” exemption without naming a figure.

Awkward timing

Congress is in recess until after the November 3 midterms. When members return, they will have a lame-duck session measured in weeks, and crypto taxes compete with government funding and whatever else leadership decides to clear before the 119th Congress ends. 

Lummis, the Senate’s loudest voice on digital asset taxes, retires in January 2027.

The Clarity Act’s collapse shapes all of this. The market structure bill passed the House 294-134 in July 2025, then stalled in the Senate for more than a year while the banking lobby fought the crypto industry over stablecoin yield and Democrats pressed for ethics language aimed at the Trump family’s crypto ventures. 

The cloture vote on September 15 failed 49-50. No Democrat crossed over, and Republicans Susan Collins, Josh Hawley and Jerry Moran voted no. Sen. Thom Tillis switched his vote so he could file a motion to reconsider, which keeps the bill alive on paper and little more.

With market structure off the table, the industry has shifted its lobbying to what might move. Tax is the obvious candidate: the House package cleared committee with bipartisan votes, and the wash sale provisions raise revenue, which gives tax writers a reason to attach them to a larger vehicle. Punchbowl News reported Thursday that the association’s refusal to back either bill signals the industry wants more than what Congress has produced.

Regulators keep filling the gap in the meantime. The OCC issued its final GENIUS Act rule on Wednesday, and the SEC and CFTC have been setting market structure policy through rulemaking and enforcement in the absence of a statute.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bitwise Asks SEC To Protect Funds Relying On Token Status Filings
summary: Bitwise filed a supplemental SEC comment seeking clearer protection for firms that rely on token-status filings. The October 21 letter develops its earlier proposal; it is an industry request, not an adopted rule.
content:
TL;DR: Bitwise filed a supplemental SEC comment seeking clearer protection for firms that rely on token-status filings. The October 21 letter develops its earlier proposal; it is an industry request, not an adopted rule.

Bitwise is pressing the Securities and Exchange Commission to answer a question that matters to fund managers: when can a firm rely on somebody else’s determination that a crypto asset has separated from an investment contract?

The asset manager’s October 21 supplemental letter focuses on that reliance problem in the SEC’s proposed Regulation Crypto Assets framework.

It asks the commission to distinguish an issuer’s filing of Form TR from the point at which a separate market participant can rely on an unchallenged filing. It also seeks protection for reasonable, good-faith determinations if a later challenge arises, and asks for the treatment to carry through relevant investment-company and investment-adviser definitions.

A Token Issuer And A Fund Manager Have Different Information

Bitwise’s original October 19 response explains its position as a company that builds investment products using crypto assets rather than issuing those assets itself. Whether an asset could be treated as a security affects decisions about which products can hold it.

The practical concern is that a manager may need to make those decisions using public information, without access to all the records held by an issuer or development team.

A reliance framework would define when public filings can support that decision and what knowledge would prevent a firm from relying on them. That is distinct from declaring that any particular token is outside securities law.

The supplement also argues that filing Form TR should not itself be treated as an admission about the asset’s previous legal status. Its requests concern the consequences of using the proposed process, not simply the form’s availability.

The Letter Does Not Resolve The Rulemaking

The document is hosted in the SEC’s comment file, but its arguments belong to Bitwise. Publication there is not an endorsement by the commission.

The distinction is especially relevant to headlines about regulatory certainty. An industry participant can identify a problem and propose a detailed solution while the outcome remains undecided.

For fund managers, the issue to watch in the eventual rules is how responsibility is divided between the party making a token-status filing and the firms using it to construct financial products. Bitwise’s latest submission makes that division the center of its case.

title: Winklevoss PAC moves into Texas Senate race with $81K ad buy
summary: While crypto-aligned PACs have stepped up spending in Ohio, a committee launched by the co-founders of crypto exchange Gemini made one of its first forays into the Lone Star State.
content:
Digital Freedom Fund, the Super political action committee (PAC) launched by Gemini co-founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2025, announced additional expenditures for US Senate races in the 2026 midterm elections, attempting to influence voters in Texas, Iowa and Ohio.

In a Tuesday filing with the US Federal Election Commission (FEC), the Digital Freedom Fund reported its first spending on ads to support Republican candidate Ken Paxton for one of Texas’ Senate seats. According to the PAC, it had spent more than $81,000 on direct mail media to support Paxton and oppose Democratic candidate James Talarico, with early voting having already begun in the state.

The Winklevoss-backed Super PAC, which reported raising about $34 million as of Sept. 30, did not limit its spending to Texas, reporting involvement in other key midterm election races using ads. Digital Freedom Fund disclosed additional expenditures in Ohio’s Senate race between Republican Jon Husted and Democrat Sherrod Brown, bringing the PAC’s total support for Husted to about $7 million.

The expenditures into candidates that could support crypto policies and laws come as event contracts on prediction market platforms Kalshi and Polymarket heavily favored Democrats retaking majority control of the House of Representatives and Senate in 2027. Whichever party holds a majority in each chamber would have a significant impact on passing legislation like the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, a market structure bill that failed to pass a procedural vote in the Senate last month.

Related: PACs laud Texas primary wins, look to back more pro-crypto candidates

Paxton already benefitted from $500,000 in supportive ads ahead of the May Republican primary, in which he defeated incumbent Senator John Cornyn. The ads, funded by the Anchorage Digital- and Cantor Fitzgerald-backed Fellowship PAC, went through the Nxum Group, a marketing company co-founded by Bo Hines, a former crypto adviser to US President Donald Trump who became CEO of Tether US after leaving the White House.

According to an October Wall Street Journal report, Nxum profited from Hines’ role in government, as he helped push a stablecoin bill while keeping a stake in the company. Nxum reportedly received $6.3 million as part of a deal with stablecoin issuer Tether, the first payment of which went through while Hines was still at the White House.

Early voting began in Texas on Oct. 19, with Election Day coming up on Nov. 3. Cointelegraph reached out to the Talarico and Paxton campaign teams for comment but did not receive an immediate response.

Spending escalates in Ohio Senate race with Fairshake PAC

Fairshake, a separate PAC aligned with the interests of the crypto industry and largely funded by Ripple Labs, Coinbase and Andreessen Horowitz, reported more than $13 million combined in spending on a direct mail campaign to support what it considered to be “pro-crypto” candidates this week. The PAC’s latest FEC filing showed more than $4 million to oppose Independent candidate Dan Osborn in Nebraska’s Senate race and an additional $9 million to support Husted over Brown.

While the battle for Ohio’s Senate between Brown and Husted has seen significant spending by PACs — Fairshake had invested about $56 million as of Wednesday and Digital Freedom Fund reported $7 million in total media purchases — Texas races have also spawned interest from Republican donors looking to prevent the state potentially losing Senate and gubernatorial seats to Democrats for the first time in more than 30 years. 

FEC filings showed that Elon Musk, the world’s richest person and founder of SpaceX, had poured more than $150 million into the Senate Leadership Fund. The PAC, supporting Republican Senate candidates, sent the same amount Musk donated to the Texas PAC, which has supported Paxton through ads.

title: MoonPay And Dunamu Explore Stablecoin Payments And GIWA Expansion
summary: MoonPay and Dunamu are exploring stablecoin payments, corporate treasury services and broader access to GIWA. Their announcement describes work to assess opportunities, with no commercial launch date disclosed.
content:
TL;DR: MoonPay and Dunamu are exploring stablecoin payments, corporate treasury services and broader access to GIWA. Their announcement describes work to assess opportunities, with no commercial launch date disclosed.

MoonPay and South Korean exchange operator Dunamu are examining how their infrastructure could support cross-border payments and corporate finance using digital assets.

The companies outlined the collaboration in a MoonPay-issued announcement distributed late Tuesday in New York, at midnight entering October 21 in London.

Three areas are on the agenda: stablecoin-based payments and fund transfers, corporate finance and treasury operations, and international expansion of Dunamu’s GIWA blockchain ecosystem.

The proposed work combines MoonPay’s financial-service network with Dunamu’s technology and business capabilities. It includes assessing commercial opportunities and ways to broaden access to GIWA-based services and assets.

Exploration Comes Before A Payment Service

The wording is deliberately preliminary. The release does not announce a jointly launched payment product, a settlement-volume commitment or a date when corporate customers can begin using a new service.

That matters because the business problem spans more than transferring a token. A company making an international payment needs to know who receives it, which currency the recipient gets, what records its finance team can reconcile and what happens if a payment fails.

Treasury management adds another layer. Businesses must decide when balances are available, which counterparties hold them and how transactions fit into their existing controls. A working blockchain connection answers only some of those questions.

MoonPay and Dunamu’s announcement identifies these corporate uses as areas to investigate. It does not show that the practical, commercial and regulatory arrangements have all been resolved.

GIWA’s overseas reach is a separate part of the proposed collaboration. Access to a distribution network can make services easier to reach, but it should not be confused with evidence that those services have already attracted customers in new markets.

For now, the announcement establishes the scope of the relationship. The next substantive step would be a named product or deployment with defined users, availability and operating terms.

title: China Moves to Confiscate $5 Billion in Bitcoin From Fraudster Who Fled to UK: Report
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

China Moves to Confiscate $5 Billion in Bitcoin From Fraudster Who Fled to UK: Report
The alleged fraudster tried to run away with nearly 62,000 bitcoins. 
This post China Moves to Confiscate $5 Billion in Bitcoin From Fraudster Who Fled to UK: Report first appeared on Bitcoin Maga...
content:
Chinese authorities are working to seize nearly 62,000 bitcoins — worth around $5 billion at today’s prices — linked to one of the country’s largest-ever fraud cases.

Prosecutors allege that Qian Zhimin, the alleged controller of Tianjin Lantian Gerui Electronic Technology, recruited associates to sell fake wealth management products nationwide from 2014 to 2017 without financial regulatory approval, promising guaranteed returns to investors, according to a report last week from Shanghai’s The Paper. 

The scheme raised some RMB 40.3 billion ($2.8 billion). Qian allegedly used investors’ cash to pay off earlier participants — Ponzi-style — while channeling funds into the bitcoin holdings, property, cars, and jewelry. Little of the money went toward legitimate business operations.

In July 2017, as the scheme unraveled, Qian fled to the UK carrying computers holding the bitcoin wallets. British authorities later seized the crypto assets and other property, including roughly 61,900 BTC along with cash, jewelry, and other cryptocurrencies. 

The case took a significant turn recently when the UK High Court ruled that Chinese law — not UK law — applies to ownership disputes over the seized bitcoin. 

The coins have appreciated enormously since 2017, and the applicable law determines whether victims share in those gains. The UK’s Crown Prosecution Service says victims may recover losses through China’s compensation mechanism, but representatives from Fieldfisher law firm, acting for some victims, are considering an appeal. Further hearings will determine whether victims can prove their entitlement to the assets.

Meanwhile, the Second Intermediate People’s Court of Tianjin announced it accepted the prosecution’s application on September 28 to confiscate Qian’s illicit assets. 

Victims can register to participate in asset recovery proceedings through a WeChat platform, with a six-month notice period before the formal trial begins.

China has some of the world’s strictest rules in regulating crypto. Its government banned digital asset trading and bitcoin mining back in 2021.

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: BitGo Launches Labs Unit With AI-Powered Gokubu Consumer App
summary: BitGo has launched a research and product unit focused initially on AI and crypto. Its first projects include Gokubu, a consumer financial app that BitGo says is already live.
content:
TL;DR: BitGo has launched a research and product unit focused initially on AI and crypto. Its first projects include Gokubu, a consumer financial app that BitGo says is already live.

BitGo is moving further into the application business with a new unit intended to build products on top of its digital-asset infrastructure.

The company announced BitGo Labs on October 21, describing an initial focus on the intersection of artificial intelligence and crypto. The unit will develop applications and publish research, prototypes and reference implementations.

Its launch includes Gokubu, which BitGo describes as a consumer app combining an AI-assisted card, a personalized financial assistant and automated rewards features. BitGo says the product is live and accepts registrations.

From Financial Infrastructure To A Consumer Product

The move puts a different kind of execution challenge alongside custody and other infrastructure services. An application must persuade users that its convenience is worth adopting, then deliver that convenience consistently.

For an AI-assisted financial product, usefulness also depends on the boundary between suggestions and actions. Showing someone a possible saving is different from making a transaction on their behalf. Permissions, clear account information and understandable costs are part of the product experience, not details that can be left to the technology underneath.

BitGo’s announcement makes ambitious claims about the role crypto infrastructure could play in an economy of autonomous software agents. Those claims describe its strategy. They do not establish that the emerging applications have already generated material revenue or reached a particular scale.

Similarly, the release’s description of Gokubu does not provide a complete account of fees, jurisdictional eligibility or the terms governing every advertised benefit. Readers should treat it as a launch announcement rather than a review of the service.

The meaningful development is that BitGo has assigned a dedicated team to turn its infrastructure into applications and named an initial consumer product. Whether that approach creates a lasting business will depend on the behavior of those products in use, including how clearly they handle the financial decisions customers entrust to them.

Geneva, Switzerland, October 22, 2026 — TRON reinforced its position as a leading blockchain network for stablecoin settlement in the third quarter of 2026, with trillions in transaction volume, record USDT supply, growing payment card adoption, and the debut of the first U.S. spot staked TRX exchange-traded fund (ETF), according to independent research reports from CoinDesk Data and Nansen.

CoinDesk 

CoinDesk’s TRON Network Quarterly Report: Q3 2026 provides a technical assessment of the TRON network from July to September 2026. The findings span network and ecosystem developments, core on-chain metrics, and DeFi activity across lending and decentralized exchanges (DEX).

Key Insights from CoinDesk:

  • Stablecoin Settlement: TRON accounted for approximately 73% of stablecoin transfer volume at the end of Q3 2026, the highest share among blockchain networks.
  • Stablecoin Market Share & USDT Growth: USDT on TRON reached an all-time high of just over $92.7 billion in Q3 2026, lifting TRON’s share of the total USDT market to a 2026 high of 50.6% in mid-September. TRON’s share of total stablecoin market capitalization also rose to 30.2%. 
  • Crypto-Card Payments & DeFi Activity: TRON ranked first among chains by crypto-card payment volume in Q3 2026, capturing a 27.5% share worth approximately $638 million as total card volumes grew 60.5% QoQ to $2.32 billion. Total value locked (TVL) on the network rose 26.6% QoQ to $5.7 billion with lending the largest sector at 68%, and JustLend active loans up from $127M to $199M.

Read the full report from CoinDesk here.

Nansen

Nansen’s TRON Quarterly Report: Q3 2026 examines the network’s settlement scale and on-chain behavior over the quarter. It covers stablecoin settlement volume, transaction and address activity, institutional developments, and how users and transactions are distributed across labeled entities on TRON.

Key Insights from Nansen:

  • Stablecoin Settlement at Scale: TRON settled $2.21 trillion in stablecoins in Q3 2026, with average daily settlement rising 3.9% to $24.05 billion. Cumulative transaction volume on the network also surpassed $30 trillion as of September 23.
  • User Growth & On-Chain Activity: TRON’s user base continued to grow in Q3 2026, with average rolling monthly active addresses up 9.8% QoQ to 18 million, while the network processed an average of 11.68 million successful transactions per day.
  • Expanded Institutional Access: Canary Capital launched the Canary Staked TRX ETF (TRXS), the first U.S. spot staked TRX ETF, on September 9, and TRON DAO rang the Cboe closing bell on September 29 to mark its debut. Anchorage Digital also added native TRX staking and TRC-20 custody as the second phase of its TRON integration.

Read the full report from Nansen here. 

Across both reports, TRON’s third quarter showed a network growing in volume and in reach at the same time. Stablecoin settlement continued to climb, everyday spending through crypto cards accelerated, and new regulated products gave institutions a direct path to TRX. With that foundation in place, TRON enters the final quarter of 2026 as a settlement network that is increasingly accessible to retail users and institutions alike.

About TRON DAO

TRON DAO is a community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet via blockchain technology and dApps.

Founded in September 2017, the TRON blockchain has experienced significant growth since its MainNet launch in May 2018. Today, TRON hosts the largest circulating supply of USD Tether (USDT) stablecoin, which currently exceeds $94 billion. As of October 2026, the TRON blockchain has recorded over 410 million in total user accounts, more than 15 billion in total transactions, and over $28 billion in total value locked (TVL), based on TRONSCAN. Recognized as the global settlement layer for stablecoin transactions and everyday purchases with proven success, TRON is “Moving Trillions, Empowering Billions.”

title: Dogecoin Labs Brings MyDoge And DogeOS Together In Commercial Reset
summary: Dogecoin Labs is bringing wallet, payment and application teams into one organization. House of Doge says it will contribute operations for an equity stake while retaining rights tied to investment products.
content:
TL;DR: Dogecoin Labs is bringing wallet, payment and application teams into one organization. House of Doge says it will contribute operations for an equity stake while retaining rights tied to investment products.

Dogecoin’s commercial development is getting a new organizational structure, with consumer products and application infrastructure being brought together under Dogecoin Labs.

House of Doge announced definitive agreements on Wednesday to contribute selected operations and assets in exchange for an equity stake. The arrangement links its product and engineering capabilities with MyDoge, DogeOS and the Such App payments business.

The release names Jordan Jefferson as Dogecoin Labs’ chief executive and identifies Alex Lewis and Dogecoin Foundation director Tim Stebbing among its leadership. It does not disclose the size of House of Doge’s equity holding.

A New Division Of Responsibilities

House of Doge says its previous exclusive commercial agreement with the Dogecoin Foundation has been replaced by a long-term license. It retains rights for its collaboration with 21Shares on Dogecoin investment products and for future tokenized alternative investments. Dogecoin Labs becomes the Foundation’s official commercial partner.

That separates two kinds of expansion. One is developing services that people use with DOGE. The other is building financial products and businesses around the asset. Bringing them under the same headline does not make their revenue models or users identical.

For developers, closer coordination could reduce the friction between a wallet’s distribution, a payment product’s merchant relationships and an application layer’s technical capabilities. A feature becomes more useful when people can discover it, fund it and use it without moving through several disconnected products.

The organizational change still has to produce that result. Combining teams does not by itself establish active usage, merchant acceptance or the security properties of future applications.

Nor is Wednesday’s agreement a change to Dogecoin’s underlying monetary rules. It is a corporate and product-development arrangement around the network.

The next evidence of its effect should come from delivered integrations and repeat usage across those products. The immediate news is the consolidation of commercial responsibility and the new relationship between the organizations building around DOGE.

title: Underdog taps zerohash to bring crypto deposits to prediction markets
summary: The new funding option, expected to launch later this year, will allow eligible Underdog users to deposit digital assets around the clock.
content:
Prediction market operator Underdog has partnered with crypto infrastructure provider zerohash to introduce cryptocurrency and stablecoin deposits, with the new funding option expected to launch later this year.

Eligible users will be able to fund their accounts directly through the Underdog app using supported digital assets, with the service designed to enable near-instant transfers around the clock, according to a Thursday announcement.

Underdog did not specify which cryptocurrencies or stablecoins would be supported and did not respond to Cointelegraph’s request for clarification before publication.

The new funding option will supplement existing methods, including debit and credit cards, Apple Pay and bank transfers. Users will not need to manage wallet addresses or select blockchain networks when making deposits.

Founded in 2020, Underdog has more than 11 million registered accounts, according to IG Group, which agreed in July to acquire the company in a deal worth up to $1.3 billion. The transaction is expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027.

According to DeFiRate data, the company recorded $1.4 billion in trading volume over the 30 days ending Oct. 21, a 133% increase from the previous period, though it remained well behind Kalshi’s $81.5 billion and the combined $17.2 billion recorded by Polymarket’s US and international platforms.

title: Tesla’s $TSLA Stock Token Lands on Solana Across 10+ Apps via Backpack Securities
summary:
Key Takeaways: Tesla’s $TSLA tokenized stock has debuted on the Solana network via Sunrise, while the issuer is listed as Backpack Securities. The token can be accessed via +10 Solana
The post Tesla’s $TSLA Stock Token Lands on Solana Across 10+ Apps via Backpack Securities appeared first on CryptoN...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Tesla’s $TSLA tokenized stock has debuted on the Solana network via Sunrise, while the issuer is listed as Backpack Securities.
  • The token can be accessed via +10 Solana applications: Phantom, Jupiter, Raydium, Kamino.
  • The launch opens the door to a novel method of tokenizing assets, bringing mainstream capital investment into the blockchain trading system.

Tesla stock has reached another side of the crypto market, and now a tokenized $TSLA exists on Solana. The launch will allow users to begin trading the asset in more than just brokerage apps, bringing tokenized equities beyond the walls of just brokerage platforms.

  • Tesla’s $TSLA Token Arrives on Solana
  • Ten Solana Apps Add Support for $TSLA
    • Wallet Access Meets Onchain Trading
    • Tokenized Stocks Expand Solana’s Crypto Market

Tesla’s $TSLA Token Arrives on Solana

Solana announced the launch on X, confirming that $TSLA is available through Sunrise and issued by Backpack Securities. The announcement also directed users to the Solana token directory to verify the asset’s contract address.

BREAKING: $TSLA is live on Solana via @sunrise, issued by @Backpack Securities https://t.co/VI8bODrEP7

— Solana (@solana) October 20, 2026

It is for this reason that it must be noted that it is a tokenized vehicle of Tesla stock, and not a token directly offered by Tesla.

In addition to its electric car efforts, Tesla is known for its energy storage solutions and autonomous driving and robotics technology. It is a popular and well-known name among investors and is a well-known stock on platforms looking to connect the blockchain to traditional financial assets. The companies agree to bring $TSLA exposure to Solana via crypto-native applications.

Read More: Securitize Puts 12 U.S. Stocks on Solana With 1:1 Backing and 24/7 Trading Plans

Ten Solana Apps Add Support for $TSLA

The list of platforms was given in the announcement where users can get the token. They include Phantom, Jupiter Exchange, Raydium, Titan Exchange, Fomo, dFlow, Archer Exchange, Meteora, Kamino Swap, and Mayan.

Wallet Access Meets Onchain Trading

This distribution has involved embedding the token in various aspects of the Solana ecosystem, including wallets and decentralized trading platforms. Access to the asset is provided via supported applications and not necessarily through a dedicated application.

But not all platforms have the same trading environment. Some venues can have liquidity, execution prices, fees, and access restrictions variations. Users must verify the market and confirm the token address prior to transacting.

According to the official announcement of Solana, the contract is called TSLAqBbv4CNCnzWFeB7LmydAyEiNMJtve7DYKLpdK4S. Confirms the entire address as there may be multiple unrelated tokens with the same ticker.

Tokenized Stocks Expand Solana’s Crypto Market

This launch brings another financial asset that is traditional to its portfolios to Solana’s expanding suite of blockchain solutions. Through tokenization, financial instruments and crypto wallets and onchain applications could become more easily foreseen in digital asset markets.

Tokenized equities also can help crypto exchange platforms appeal to customers who aren’t blockchain fans but have an interest in traditional asset categories. But their utility relies on legal rights that are associated with each token, arrangements, liquidity, and rules that determine eligible investors.

The $TSLA token is now available and will be trading on a much broader range of Solana applications. The future growth of adoption will depend on the success of trading, accessing users, and the value the token provides after its launch.

title: Barclays Plans 5,000 Job Cuts by 2026 in AI Efficiency Drive Despite £2.3B Profit and £500M Share Buyback
summary: Barclays plans to cut approximately 5,000 jobs by the end of 2026 as the British banking group expands its use of artificial intelligence (AI) to reduce costs and improve operational efficiency.
content:
Skip to content

Barclays plans to cut approximately 5,000 jobs by the end of 2026 as the British banking group expands its use of artificial intelligence (AI) to reduce costs and improve operational efficiency.

The planned reductions represent around 5% of Barclays’ global workforce, despite the bank reporting higher quarterly profits and announcing a £500 million share buyback.

Around 1,000 positions have already been eliminated, with most cuts targeting UK operational and support functions, including software development roles. The announcement comes as Barclays reports stronger equities trading revenue, while rising costs and regulatory concerns remain among the challenges facing the bank.

Barclays Targets 5,000 Jobs in AI-Driven Restructuring

Barclays described the initiative in its earnings presentation as “organisational simplification and technology change efficiency driven by AI.” The programme aims to streamline operations and improve productivity by integrating AI into existing business processes.

Sky News reports that Barclays plans to cut 5,000 jobs, around 5% of its workforce, as it invests in AI to streamline back-office operations, reduce costs, and improve efficiency. Source: @SkyNews via X

Approximately 60% of the planned job losses will affect support functions, including technology and software development teams. AI tools can automate routine tasks and assist employees with coding and other operational work, potentially reducing the staffing required for certain activities.

Most reductions are expected to affect operational and functional roles in the UK. With around 1,000 positions already eliminated, Barclays plans to complete the remaining cuts by the end of 2026.

Barclays Reports £2.3 Billion Quarterly Profit

The job-cut announcement coincided with Barclays’ third-quarter financial results. The bank reported approximately £2.3 billion in profit before tax, up around 12% year over year.

Profit after tax increased to £1.65 billion from £1.46 billion in the same period a year earlier, representing growth of approximately 13%. Total group income rose 3% to £7.37 billion, supported by stronger performance in its investment banking division.

Barclays posted £2.3 billion in Q3 profit, up 12% year-over-year, and launched a £500 million buyback, signaling efficiency-driven cuts rather than financial distress. Source: @Elizacreatez via X

Equities trading was a key contributor, with revenue from the business increasing 47% year-over-year.

Chief executive C. S. Venkatakrishnan highlighted the bank’s continuing operational and financial performance, pointing to strong results from the investment bank’s equities business.

However, higher profits have not eliminated concerns about costs and performance relative to market expectations. The results show that Barclays is pursuing workforce reductions while remaining profitable, rather than responding solely to immediate financial distress.

£500 Million Share Buyback Adds to Shareholder Returns

Barclays also announced a £500 million share buyback, through which the bank will repurchase its own shares. Buybacks return capital to shareholders and can increase earnings per share by reducing the number of shares outstanding.

The restructuring carries reported costs of approximately £501 million, reflecting expenses associated with implementing organizational changes. Although these costs can weigh on short-term results, lower payroll expenses could reduce operating costs over time if the planned efficiencies materialize.

The simultaneous announcement of job cuts and a share buyback has drawn attention to Barclays’ approach to cost management and shareholder returns. However, the available figures do not establish that the buyback is being funded directly by workforce reductions.

Barclays CEO Frames AI as an Enhancement to Existing Technology

Venkatakrishnan previously described AI as “the icing on the cake, not the cake” in a September interview with Bloomberg, emphasizing its role within the bank’s broader technology infrastructure.

Barclays CEO C.S. Venkatakrishnan called AI “the icing on the cake, not the cake,” with 1,000 roles already cut and remaining reductions targeted by year-end. Source: @vig_says via X

Barclays is incorporating AI into existing processes rather than presenting it as a wholesale replacement for its technology systems. Potential applications include software development, document processing, and data analysis, where automation can reduce manual workloads.

The planned reductions in support and development roles illustrate how AI adoption is affecting technical as well as administrative work. Banks must still maintain skilled teams to oversee automated systems, protect sensitive data, and meet regulatory requirements.

Costs and Regulatory Concerns Remain in Focus

AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould said Barclays’ third-quarter performance had fallen short of market expectations, adding that the share buyback had not fully eased investor disappointment.

Mould also pointed to rising group costs and two concerns for shareholders: a potential increase in taxes on the UK banking sector in the government’s upcoming budget and a reported investigation into possible misrepresentation of risks in the bank’s private credit portfolio.

Both issues could affect investor sentiment and the bank’s financial outlook. Any impact from taxation or the reported investigation will depend on subsequent policy decisions and the outcome of the relevant proceedings.

AI-Driven Job Cuts Signal a Shift in Banking Operations

Barclays’ restructuring reflects the growing use of AI to streamline operations across financial services. Banks are exploring automation to improve productivity and manage expenses, with software development and back-office work increasingly among the areas affected.

For Barclays, the key test will be whether the changes deliver lasting cost savings while preserving the technical expertise and oversight needed to operate a large financial institution. The bank has until the end of 2026 to complete the planned workforce reductions.

The announcement also highlights the employment implications of AI adoption. As banks integrate automation into routine workflows, the technology is reshaping staffing requirements even at profitable institutions. The longer-term effects will depend on how effectively companies translate productivity gains into sustainable operational improvements.

title: Utexo Opens Utexo Mint Early Access for USDT on Bitcoin Ahead of November 28 Launch
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Utexo Opens Utexo Mint Early Access for USDT on Bitcoin Ahead of November 28 Launch
Utexo has opened Utexo Mint, letting verified professional operators test minting, confidential transfers, and redemption of USDT on Bitcoin via RGB ahead of the November 28 public launch.
This post...
content:
Professional operators can now test USDT on Bitcoin and get their integrations ready for November’s public launch.

Utexo has opened Utexo Mint, its dedicated platform for professional operators preparing to support and offer USDT on Bitcoin. The public launch is scheduled for November 28.

The return of USDT creates an opportunity to bring dollar liquidity into the Bitcoin ecosystem, opening new markets for trading and BTC-backed lending. Operators who integrate early can be among the first to offer USDT on Bitcoin, “positioning themselves to capture initial demand and build market share as adoption grows,” according to a press release shared with Bitcoin Magazine.

Utexo says existing partners are already preparing for the launch, as it is opening onboarding to exchanges, wallets, market makers, OTC desks, trading firms, and other professional operators interested in supporting USDT on Bitcoin.

Utexo Mint

Utexo Mint is a dedicated platform for verified operators to mint and redeem USDT on Bitcoin.

Within its sandbox environment, operators can test how USDT works on Bitcoin via RGB, including “minting, confidential transfers, and redemption.” The testing period should give operators time to validate their transaction flows and finalize their integrations ahead of the launch.

Utexo said they will also offer tools to manage USDT liquidity across supported networks and convert between fiat and USDT, giving operators greater flexibility in how they source and move funds. While Utxo Mint is not owned or operated by Tether, USDT on Bitcoin is nevertheless backed by USDT via Tether’s USDT0 protocol.

Bringing USDT Back Home to Bitcoin

USDT is returning to Bitcoin, where it first launched in 2014, bringing deep stablecoin liquidity to the ecosystem and expanding what businesses can do on the network. USDT on Bitcoin is launched by Utexo and not by Tether, the company clarified.

USDT on Bitcoin will be “private by design,” said the press release, allowing individuals to hold and transfer funds without publicly exposing their transaction details. Among the various technology differences between its Bitcoin implementation and that on EVM blockchains, RGB’s USDT avoids address reuse, the worst privacy practice and one which may even expose holders to quantum computer risks.

When it comes to compliance, the press release said businesses will be able to protect sensitive commercial activity while maintaining the controls required for regulatory compliance. When asked how privacy and compliance with sanctions and law enforcement can be offered as features at the same time, Utxo told Bitcoin Magazine, “We monitor all source USDT coming in, and check AML score + we monitor the risk on the RGB side too. We have a partnership with Crystal Intelligence for the AML”

The rollout will take place in two phases. The first begins on November 28, when USDT becomes publicly available on the Bitcoin network via RGB. The launch will make it accessible through partner wallets and exchanges, introducing new liquidity for swap providers and lending platforms.

The second phase, planned for Q1 2027, will extend USDT to the Lightning Network for payments, according to Utexo.

title: Bitcoin Slides Towards $81,000 as Oil Above $110 Revives Rate-Hike Bets
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Slides Towards $81,000 as Oil Above $110 Revives Rate-Hike Bets
Bitcoin is currently in so-called Uptober, a month when the asset is supposed to rally. But it’s being held back — at least for now. 
This post Bitcoin Slides Towards $81,000 as Oil Above $110 Revives Rate-Hike...
content:
Bitcoin’s price on Thursday slid — erasing the gains it made earlier in the week — after oil prices jumped. 

The largest cryptocurrency was down by nearly 4% over a 24-hour period on Thursday in New York, trading as low as $81,331 at one point. 

On Wednesday, the price of the top cryptocurrency was fast closing in on $85,000 as investors piled back into tech stocks following Elon Musk’s SpaceX earnings. 

But conflict in the Middle East pushed the oil price higher, spurring inflation fears with U.S. A surging oil price can — at least in the short-term — hurt the price of bitcoin and other “risk-on” assets because it increases the chances of the U.S. central bank raising interest rates. 

Bitcoin has in the past done well with low interest rates because of increased liquidity, moving at times with tech stocks and the Nasdaq. 

Stocks on Thursday slid on the news of more attacks from the Yemeni Houthis on Saudi Arabia — stoked fears of oil supply disruptions and a wider Middle East conflict.

Bitcoin has typically faced downward pressure on news of war and rallied in hopes of a ceasefire. 

When the U.S. and Israel first attacked Iran in February, the coin nosedived, and had been shaky on news of war in March and April. 

Oil rising is stoking what many politicians are calling an affordability crisis in the U.S. Americans will go to the polls on November 3, and surging inflation is one of the hottest topics. 

The Federal Reserve has said getting inflation down in the world’s largest economy is its top priority. 

Despite the price of bitcoin dipping, the asset just had its best quarter in years, and analysts have said the coin is now in a bull market after rising above its 365-day moving average. 

Bitcoin last month shrugged off the Federal Reserve raising interest rates and lawmakers blocking landmark crypto legislation, the Clarity Act. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Irish central bank fines Coinbase Ireland $3.6 million over fund safeguarding failures
summary: When Silvergate was on the verge of collapse in 2023, Coinbase instructed 30 customers to deposit funds into an alternate account held by Coinbase at another U.S. bank.
content:
Summary

  • Ireland’s central bank fined Coinbase Ireland 3.25 million euros ($3.6 million) for alleged failures in safeguarding customer funds and overseeing outsourced services.
  • The regulator said Coinbase Ireland relied excessively on its U.S.-based parent and lacked adequate systems and controls, while Coinbase disclosed that coding errors left a safeguarding account underfunded by an average of 0.54% in 2023 and the first half of 2024.
  • Coinbase said no customers lost money or were unable to access their funds. The penalty follows a 21.4 million-euro Irish fine imposed on Coinbase Europe in 2025 for anti-money laundering failures.

Coinbase Ireland was hit with a 3.25 million-euro ($3.6 million) fine from the country’s central bank over alleged breaches of its safeguarding and outsourcing obligations.

The Irish division of cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase Global COIN$169.13·Market Closed failed to establish an adequate outsourcing governance framework, the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI) said on Thursday.

Safeguarding and outsourcing requirements underpin the protection of customer funds. Companies are obliged to keep them adequately funded and monitored and set up procedures to report to the regulator when material changes occur.

“They placed excessive reliance on the U.S.-based Coinbase Group as an outsourced service provider to implement safeguarding processes and controls [and] failed to adequately safeguard customers’ funds, both through inadequate system design and insufficient control testing,” the CBI said.

When crypto-friendly bank Silvergate was on the verge of collapse in 2023, Coinbase instructed 30 customers to deposit funds into an alternate account held by Coinbase at another U.S. bank, the company said in a statement following the CBI’s announcement.

The funds were therefore held alongside those belonging to customers of another Coinbase entity, a breach of safeguarding requirements.

Coinbase also referred to euro withdrawals from U.S. or U.K.-based customers being paid from Coinbase Ireland’s safeguarding account, and coding errors leading to the account being underfunded by an average of 0.54% in 2023 and the first half of 2024.

“No customer suffered any financial loss as a result of these matters, and no customer was ever unable to access their funds,” Coinbase said.

The penalty arrives almost one year after the CBI fined Coinbase Europe 21.4 million euros for breaching its anti-money laundering (AML) obligations between 2021 and 2025.

title: Robinhood Wins Dubai License to Bring Bitcoin and Stock Trading to the Middle East in 2027
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Robinhood Wins Dubai License to Bring Bitcoin and Stock Trading to the Middle East in 2027
Robinhood has won DFSA approval to offer bitcoin, crypto and stock trading with custody from a new Dubai headquarters, with launch set for 2027.
This post Robinhood Wins Dubai License to Brin...
content:
Robinhood Markets has received authorization from the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA) to offer retail trading and custody across 10 asset classes, including bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, equities, ETFs and investment tokens, the company said in a statement on Wednesday. 

The platform is set to go live in the region in 2027 from a new hub in the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC), a special economic zone that will serve as the firm’s Middle East and North Africa headquarters.

Salah Kaddoura has been named senior executive officer and president of Robinhood MENA. The title is a DFSA-recognized role, which makes him the person regulators will call. He will build out the Dubai team ahead of launch.

“The DIFC is one of the world’s most important financial hubs, and our expansion there brings us closer to building a global platform that enables anyone, anywhere to own the highest quality financial assets,” said Vlad Tenev, Robinhood’s chairman and CEO, in the company statement. 

Robinhood’s expansion over the years  

Dubai extends a run of expansion beyond the US, where the app made its name with young investors trading single stocks. 

Robinhood entered the UK in 2024, opened full operations in the European Union last year, won in-principle approval for brokerage services in Singapore in April, and closed its purchase of Canadian crypto platform WonderFi in June. 

At home, it added weekend trading and perpetual futures in September. The company says it counts more than one million customers outside the US.

Johann Kerbrat, who runs crypto and international for Robinhood, framed the Dubai move around a wave of new retail investors in the region. He is the same executive who disclosed on October 7 that Robinhood had put $25 million of bitcoin on its own balance sheet, the first time the firm held BTC as a corporate asset rather than on behalf of customers.

The DFSA has signed off on Robinhood holding client digital assets, not routing trades alone. For a firm that took years to enable bitcoin withdrawals in the United States, being cleared for custody from day one in a new jurisdiction says something about how far its crypto operation has matured.

Robinhood arrives in a financial center that keeps growing despite the war with Iran and tension across the region. The DIFC passed 10,000 active registered firms this year and continues to draw global names, Ken Griffin’s Citadel among them.

In March, it opened a cluster of new towers with 600,000 square feet of commercial space, with Deutsche Bank and Moody’s among the tenants, according to Bloomberg. Proprietary trading firm Maven said this week it will close its New York office as it shifts weight to Dubai.

Competition will not be thin. The DIFC listed 72 authorized brokerages as of March 31, and several crypto-native exchanges hold licenses from Dubai’s separate Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority. 

Robinhood has not said which countries will be served at launch, what pricing will look like, or how “eligible investors” will be defined, and that last point will decide the size of the addressable market.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Crypto for Advisors: Stablecoins are ready for prime time
content:
Updated Oct 22, 2026, 4:00 p.m. EDTPublished Oct 22, 2026, 10:58 a.m. EDT

6 min read

Summary

Happy Thursday, advisors!

In today’s newsletter, Prashant Kher of EY-Parthenon on what new survey data shows about where stablecoins are gaining ground, and what will decide which payment rails scale

Then, in “Ask an Expert,” Sam Boboev of Fintech WrapUp on whether euro stablecoins can challenge the dollar’s lead, and who is best placed to win on distribution.

Happy reading.

- Sarah Morton


Stablecoins are going mainstream

A year ago, the stablecoin debate centered on whether regulatory clarity and a compelling combination of speed, cost and liquidity benefits would drive meaningful adoption. The evidence now points to a market moving decisively from experimentation toward implementation.

EY-Parthenon’s 2026 Blockchain Payments Survey of 521 corporate and financial institution decision-makers found that 18% of corporates have used stablecoins in production, double the share reported in our 2025 survey. Tokenized deposits are close behind, with 15% of corporates reporting adoption.

Financial institutions are also making firm commitments. A total of 69% offer stablecoin services or plan to launch them within two years, up from 30% in 2025. Among banks, 49% already offer or plan to offer tokenized deposits over the same period.

Although blockchain payments have not yet reached mass adoption, the survey findings provide clear evidence that the market is shifting from technology trials to integrating capabilities into existing payment workflows and treasury operations.

Source: 2026 EY-Parthenon blockchain payments survey

Cross-border payments are the entry point

Cross-border business payments remain the most common use case. Across stablecoins and tokenized deposits, 50% to 53% of all respondents have used or are exploring each for cross-border supplier payments or cross-border business-to-business (B2B) payment acceptance.

Overall blockchain payments exploration & adoption

Cross-border B2B flows lead blockchain payment use cases for most respondents, while interest in payouts is concentrated among banks and payments firms.

Source: 2026 EY-Parthenon blockchain payments survey

These applications directly address frictions corporates experience in cross-border payments. A total of 56% cite slow processing and settlement; 52% cite foreign exchange costs or spreads; 48% cite regulatory, sanctions and compliance delays; and 36% cite correspondent banking fees. Financial institutions see the corresponding opportunity, with faster settlement and lower costs ranking among the leading drivers of interest in both stablecoins and tokenized deposits.

The opportunity extends beyond basic money movement. Tokenized asset settlement was the most frequently selected opportunity to add value on top of blockchain payment rails, cited by 63% of respondents from financial institutions, reflecting strong interest in using blockchain-based money as a settlement mechanism.

The market is becoming multi-rail

Adoption is moving beyond a binary choice between stablecoins and tokenized deposits. Among respondents with an interest in blockchain payments, 45% of corporates and 53% of financial institutions favor using both rails. Respondents cite flexibility and the expectation that the two methods will coexist as leading reasons, suggesting that different payment needs will call for different forms of digital money.

That preference reflects the different roles the two methods can play. Stablecoins provide reach across wallets, platforms and public blockchain networks, while tokenized deposits can bring commercial bank money into programmable environments. Rather than selecting a single rail, organizations can choose between them based on the use case, counterparty, geography and liquidity requirements.

For financial institutions and payment providers, the opportunity is to make that choice seamless for clients, enabling them to move between payment methods, both traditional fiat and blockchain payments, through integrated processes and a unified experience.

Integration and programmability will determine what scales

Corporate expectations favor embedded delivery of blockchain payment services. A total of 76% consider integration with existing enterprise resource planning, treasury management and banking platforms very important or critical. In addition, 74% want blockchain payments fully integrated into existing banking and payment interfaces, while only 14% prefer a separate experience for digital assets.

That preference creates an advantage for incumbent providers: 63% of corporates would likely adopt blockchain payments if offered by their existing bank or payments provider. However, financial institutions must build on trusted relationships with credible economics, secure execution and regulatory readiness.

Programmability represents a separate but complementary opportunity to create value. A total of 54% of financial institutions already offer or plan to launch programmable payments within two years, and 75% view them as at least a moderate revenue opportunity. For financial institutions, the leading priorities for programmable payments include liquidity and cash management automation at 51%, conditional payments at 51%, automated reconciliation at 49% and cross-border automation at 47%.

Source: 2026 EY-Parthenon blockchain payments survey

Outlook

Blockchain payment adoption may increasingly occur inside familiar banking and payment products, rather than through stand-alone digital asset interfaces. Institutions that integrate stablecoins, tokenized deposits and traditional rails into existing workflows, while adding programmable services above those rails, will be best positioned to lead the next phase of adoption.

Disclaimer: The views expressed in this article are those of the author and not necessarily those of Ernst & Young LLP or other members of the EY global organization.

- Prashant Kher, partner, EY-Parthenon

Ask an Expert
Q. Why are payment companies launching their own stablecoins, such as OUSD, and how could this change their business models?

  1. Payment companies are increasingly interested in issuing stablecoins because they see an opportunity to capture more value from the money moving through their platforms.

Today, payment providers generate revenue primarily through transaction fees, currency conversion and other financial services. Issuing a stablecoin could create an additional revenue stream from the reserves backing tokens in circulation, subject to the applicable regulatory framework.

There is also a strategic benefit. A payment company with its own stablecoin could connect merchant settlements, cross-border payouts and customer balances within a single infrastructure.

This could reduce dependence on external settlement providers and improve liquidity management.

However, distribution will be critical. Issuing a stablecoin is relatively straightforward compared with convincing businesses to hold and use it.

I expect payment companies with established merchant networks and strong distribution to have an advantage. Their existing customer relationships could help them turn stablecoins into practical payment products.

Q. Why are banking consortia in the U.S. and Europe developing stablecoins, and how could they compete with existing issuers?

  1. Banks are increasingly concerned about losing payment flows and customer balances as stablecoin adoption grows.

In Europe, Qivalis has brought together 37 financial institutions across 15 countries to develop a regulated euro stablecoin.

Meanwhile, a separate global consortia of 21 financial institutions, including Bank of America, Citi, Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo, announced plans in September 2026 to launch a U.S. dollar stablecoin in the first half of 2027, with euro issuance also a priority.

These initiatives could allow banks to offer around-the-clock settlement while retaining their role in managing customer funds.

I see the biggest opportunity in institutional payments and tokenized asset settlement, where banks already have established customer relationships and payment infrastructure.

However, competing with existing stablecoin issuers will require sufficient liquidity and broad distribution.

The real test will be whether these consortiums can convert their existing banking relationships into meaningful transaction volumes.

Q. What is driving the push for euro-denominated stablecoins, and can they challenge the dominance of U.S. dollar stablecoins?

  1. Euro stablecoins currently represent a tiny share of the market. According to Bank of Ireland, just 0.2% of global stablecoin circulation was euro-denominated in May 2026.

This creates a problem for European businesses that want to use blockchain payments while keeping their transactions and treasury balances in euros.

Using dollar stablecoins introduces foreign exchange costs and currency exposure.

The EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation has provided a regulatory framework for euro stablecoin issuers, while European banks are developing infrastructure to support euro-denominated settlement.

I see the strongest opportunities in European B2B payments and corporate treasury.

However, challenging dollar stablecoins globally will be difficult. Dollar liquidity and established distribution networks give existing issuers a considerable advantage.

The more realistic opportunity is to build a strong euro stablecoin market serving European businesses and financial institutions.

Adoption will depend on liquidity and integration with existing banking systems.

- Sam Boboev, founder, Fintech WrapUp

title: Fireblocks Denies Report of $2.5 Billion Visa Takeover Talks
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Fireblocks Denies Report of $2.5 Billion Visa Takeover Talks
Fireblocks has denied an Axios report that Visa is in late-stage talks to acquire the crypto custody firm for about $2.5 billion.
This post Fireblocks Denies Report of $2.5 Billion Visa Takeover Talks first appeared on Bi...
content:
Fireblocks has denied a report that Visa is in late-stage talks to buy the institutional crypto custody and stablecoin infrastructure firm for around $2.5 billion.

“We are aware of the rumors about a possible acquisition of Fireblocks by Visa. This is news to us, and not true at present time,” the company told The Block on Thursday. 

The denial came hours after Axios reported, citing multiple sources, that the two sides were close to a deal. It would have been Visa’s first acquisition in the stablecoin sector and one of the largest in crypto’s history, behind Coinbase’s $2.9 billion purchase of Deribit in 2025 and Naver Financial’s pending $10.3 billion deal for Upbit parent Dunamu.

The reported price would have been a steep markdown from the $8 billion valuation Fireblocks commanded in January 2022, when it raised $550 million in a Series E round at the peak of the venture cycle. Founded in 2018 by Michael Shaulov, Pavel Berengoltz and Idan Ofrat, three veterans of the Israeli cybersecurity scene, the company sells the plumbing that banks, exchanges and fintechs use to hold and move digital assets. 

Its customers include BNY Mellon, Worldpay, Revolut and Galaxy, and it says it has secured trillions of dollars in transfers across more than 150 blockchains.

Fireblocks powers FIS’s institutional bitcoin trading, underpins BNP Paribas’s digital asset custody, and sits among the founding members of the Botanix federation, a bitcoin sidechain project.

The crypto land grab

Whatever the status of the talks, the report landed on fertile ground. Payment incumbents spent 2026 buying or courting the companies that handle stablecoin and crypto rails rather than building them from scratch. 

Mastercard agreed in March to buy BVNK for up to $1.8 billion, after takeover talks with Zerohash fell through, closed that deal in August and secured a New York BitLicense along the way. 

Zerohash, for its part, is seeking a US national trust bank charter.

Visa partnered with Zerohash in August to add stablecoin funding and payouts to Visa Direct, and in September said its stablecoin settlement volume had passed a $20 billion annualized run rate, more than 15 times the prior year’s level. 

Both card networks joined a coalition of more than 140 companies behind Open USD, a dollar stablecoin designed to spread the economics of a $300 billion market beyond Tether and Circle.

Fireblocks launched its own stablecoin payments network in September 2025 with over 40 participants, including Circle, Bridge, Zerohash and Yellow Card, and this year rolled out acceptance tools for neobanks and a settlement suite aimed at AI agents. 

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Crypto custody specialist Fireblocks denies it's in talks to be acquired by Visa
summary: The company is in talks with Visa over a potential $2.5 billion acquisition, Axios reported.
content:
Summary

  • A Fireblocks spokesperson said the acquisition talks were “news to us, and not true at present time.”
  • Fireblocks previously raised $550 million at an $8 billion valuation back in 2022.

Cryptocurrency custody firm Fireblocks dismissed reports it is in talks with Visa (V) to be acquired for $2.5 billion.

Axios, citing multiple unidentified sources, said the company was in late-stage talks with Visa.

“We are aware of the rumors about a possible acquisition of Fireblocks by Visa. This is news to us, and not true at present time,” a Fireblocks spokesperson said soon after the Axios story broke.

Fireblocks specializes in crypto custody using advanced pre-key sharding technologies such as multi-party computation (MPC).

A $2.5 billion purchase would be a marked drop in value since 2022, when Fireblocks raised $550 million at an $8 billion valuation.

That said, smoke has been circulating over the past three or four weeks about a potential sale of the business, with anonymous sources telling CoinDesk U.S.-listed Coinbase Global COIN$169.13·Market Closed was also in the frame to buy Fireblocks.

After this story was published, Coinbase denied it was involved in a possible transaction. Visa did not respond to requests for comment.

UPDATE (Oct. 22, 15:24 UTC): Adds Coinbase denial in final paragraph.
