title: Crypto is making a splash in U.S. elections — but chiefly in jabs about industry influence
summary: Boosters often say crypto voters can swing elections, but Democrats are seeking mileage out of tying crypto to Trump, corruption and attempts to buy seats in Congress.
content:
Oct 22, 2026, 9:00 a.m. EDT

6 min read

Summary

  • The crypto industry's campaign spending doesn't make ads that mention crypto, so the main place the topic has come up in the elections is as a political weapon wielded by Democrats bashing the sector and its ties to President Donald Trump.
  • Candidates such as former Senate Banking Committee Chairman Sherrod Brown and incumbent Virginia Senator Mark Warner are flagging the industry's outsized political spending and close relationship with the president.

Crypto is finally being talked about in U.S. political campaigns, but it's certainly not in a light that the industry would choose.

Though digital assets advocates have long referenced a grassroots uprising of crypto-focused voters that can swing elections, the industry's own massive campaign spending has carefully decided against even mentioning the financial technology in the ads it buys for favored candidates. But crypto is having a moment in the midterms, anyway, as the sector's critics paint its political involvement as a venal influence on congressional campaigning.

A number of Democratic candidates have raised crypto as a black mark to suggest improper corporate sway over their political adversaries and more generally as a factor in corruption accusations against President Donald Trump and his administration. In this environment, in which voters are now weighing government corruption as a top political concern, it may carry consequential weight.

In a current campaign ad from Senator Mark Warner, the Virginia Democrat seeks to tarnish Trump and his allies by highlighting the billions Trump has made in office and the jet he accepted as a gift from Qatar. The ad also notes that Trump made hundreds of millions of dollars off of his "crypto memecoin," followed by Warner saying: "That's not governing. It's grifting. The corruption needs to stop."

And in former Senator Sherrod Brown's bid to return to the Senate for Ohio, the Democrat has embraced the massive crypto spending against him as a point of favor.

"The crypto/data-center crowd are up to $40 million now," Brown, the former chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, said in a recent Pod Save America interview, noting the industry's opposition ads in Ohio were largely bankrolled by a crypto political action committee (Fairshake). "They know I'm going to hold them accountable," Brown said.

Fairshake spent tens of millions trying to get him voted out of office two years ago, and the super PAC started major spending again to keep Brown out. As a result, he offers an us-versus-them (regular voters against tech billionaires) narrative on the campaign trail. The ex-senator frequently lumps crypto and data centers together in his speeches, accusing those tech elements of trying to buy the incumbent Republican opponent Jon Husted's seat "because they know I'll never work for them," Brown said in a campaign video spot.

Oliver Gilbert, a Democrat running for Congress in Florida, has also made his crypto-world political enemies an element in his campaigning — especially after the Fairshake super PAC spent $2 million in a failed attempt to defeat him in the primaries.

"Trump and his crypto con artist billionaires just put a target on my back," he said in one ad after the industry's campaign operation came after him. Gilbert accused crypto interests of lavishing dark money to spread lies about his record, and he said he'd fight to "protect seniors from crypto scams."

Minnesota Senate candidate Peggy Flanagan and Illinois Senate candidate Juliana Stratton (another of Fairshake's most high-profile losses) both flagged their crypto friction during their primary races. Stratton posted a video describing the millions a "MAGA-backed crypto PAC" spent in attack ads against her.

The Trump midterms

Just as President Trump has urged his supporters to think of him when they vote, the congressional midterms are widely viewed as focused on his presidency. And part of that record has been his aggressive crypto push and his substantial personal benefits.

Voters are worrying about self-dealing political behavior more they have before. A Fox News poll of voters this month showed that "government corruption" was the top issue of concern, showing 88% of respondents were at least very concerned about it — higher even than inflation, gas prices and healthcare.

Many Democrats, including Warner, are insisting that the crypto industry belongs in the conversation about Trump administration corruption.

"We are getting peppered on a weekly basis on the latest way the president is trying to profit off of this," said Will Ragland, vice president of research in the advocacy department at the Center for American Progress.

Since 2024, Ragland said the industry decided to lash itself to Trump and his political allies, and a major piece of evidence is the president's primary super PAC, MAGA Inc. Crypto interests represent the leading industry contributors to the PAC, according to an analysis from his organization, noting almost $89 million in contributions from the sector, significantly outpacing other industries.

The industry’s close relationship with Trump, who controls a personal crypto empire himself, has brought some benefits to the sector, such as the crypto-friendly regulators who have dismissed enforcement actions and are writing new rules, but it may have come at a cost greater than the price tag on campaign contributions.

Crypto companies "made a very poor strategic decision early on here," Ragland said. Though they've supported candidates from both parties, the greater lean was toward Trump and congressional Republicans. "To some extent, it worked, in terms of seeing investigations dropped and having a direct line into the presidency," he said, but now the accusations against Trump (which often highlight his crypto earnings that Ragland's organization live-tracks, currently around $2.4 billion) have reached a "fever pitch."

"It didn't have to be this way for the industry," he said, predicting that it'll be "an uphill battle to climb back from."

For its part, the Blockchain Association — an advocacy group in Washington — said it’s just trying to get rules that "don't depend on who sits in the White House or who controls Congress."

“As we all know, politics has become more polarized, and industries across the spectrum have been pulled into that fight at one time or another," said the group's chief policy officer, Lindsay Fraser, in a statement. "But that doesn’t change what we push for. We’ll keep working with Democrats and Republicans alike, because our focus is on making sure the United States leads in this technology, leads in its share of developers, and leads in innovation.”

But the president's crypto connections may also have led to the failure of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act — the market structure bill that represented the industry's biggest goal in Washington. Trump's business ties to crypto contributed to demands from Democratic lawmakers that the bill include stringent ethics constraints on government officials, and what the president was willing to accept was deemed by them to be insufficient. So the bill didn't advance in the Senate last month, and its chances are slim to see further action for the rest of the year.

Spending continues

The industry's dominant super PAC, Fairshake, has spent vast sums of money on trying to get crypto-friendly candidates into Congress, counting a large majority of successes in this year's primaries. They're supporting dozens of incumbents so far in the general election, and opposing Brown with at least $40 million in what may become the most expensive congressional race in U.S. history. The many ads they've purchased nationwide focus on issues the PAC believes will sway voters, and a spokesman confirmed that the crypto group's ads don’t mention crypto, the technology that's paying for them (mostly through the contributions of Coinbase, Ripple and a16z Crypto).

For voters, crypto hasn't yet proven to be a decisive issue, as much as the industry has hoped it would be. A CoinDesk poll released in May showed crypto was very low on voters' list of priorities. (The same survey revealed people didn't trust the Trump administration to oversee digital assets.)

The crypto sector's urgent desire for a U.S. law that governs its markets now faces the November 3 elections. The outcome could shift the U.S. House of Representatives to a Democratic majority, and possibly the Senate, too. That would mean a very different experience on Capitol Hill for crypto lobbyists, and the odds get longer to pass a major bill that the crypto industry can support.

As they try to join what they hope will be a Democrat majority in the House and Senate, Democratic candidates keep banging the crypto drum. When he ran a key committee in the Senate, Brown had the authority to deflect the industry's attempts at legislation, and if he gets back in and finds himself in a similarly powerful role, the situation may be even worse.

As Brown promised in a speech earlier this month on C-SPAN, "They know I'm going to take them on."

  • On 24 November, Old Billingsgate brings together the decision-makers, industry leaders and companies shaping financial markets. With a headline Speaker Hall, curated Business Connect Roundtables, One to One meetings and one day to make the right connections, the opportunity starts with being in the room.

Some industry conversations are worth more than a dozen emails. Some introductions can change the direction of a business. And some opportunities depend on being in the right room at the right time.

On 24 November 2026, FM Summit London returns to Old Billingsgate for its 15th edition, bringing together senior professionals across online trading, institutional finance, brokerage, liquidity, trading technology, fintech, payments and digital assets. Alongside a focused conference programme, the event will feature an exhibition where sponsors and exhibitors can showcase their solutions, connect directly with potential clients, meet industry decision-makers and explore new business opportunities. Through face-to-face networking, targeted meetings and conversations across the exhibition floor, attendees can build partnerships, discover new providers and develop commercial relationships, all under one roof.

The exhibition will feature leading companies including LMAX Group, Plus500, oneZero, PLUGIT, Adaptive, ATFX, CMC Markets, MetaQuotes, Devexperts, Finalto and CXM Prime. Through the Business Connect programme, attendees can also take part in pre-arranged one-to-one meetings and invitation-only roundtables, creating more direct opportunities to discuss business needs, evaluate solutions and establish partnerships with relevant decision-makers.

As FM Summit London approaches its 15th edition, the event is shaping up to be one of its most significant gatherings yet, bringing together established industry leaders, leading companies and decision-makers for a day of business development, knowledge exchange and networking. With an exhibition floor, a focused conference programme and opportunities for targeted meetings, the summit provides a setting for professionals to explore emerging trends, identify new commercial opportunities and build relationships across the industry. For those attending on 24 November, the value lies not only in understanding where the market is heading, but also in connecting with the people and businesses helping to shape its future.

The Connections Start Before the Summit: Opening Blitz on 23 November

The experience begins a day early with the Opening Networking Blitz on 23 November 2026 at The Folly, London. This pre-event gathering gives attendees an opportunity to connect with fellow industry professionals, meet potential business partners and start building valuable relationships ahead of the main Summit on 24 November at Old Billingsgate.

Now in its 15th edition, FM Summit London brings together senior decision-makers, C-level executives and industry leaders across online trading, institutional finance, brokerage, liquidity, trading technology, fintech, payments and digital assets.

The People You Need to Meet Are Coming Together

The value of an industry summit lies in both its agenda and the people in the room.

FM Summit London 2026 brings together key players across brokerage, institutional trading, liquidity, technology and digital assets. Confirmed companies include LMAX Group, Plus500, oneZero, PLUGIT, Adaptive, Edge Hound, AEGIS Trading Technology, MetaQuotes, Devexperts, Acuity and CXM Prime.

The summit offers an opportunity to explore solutions, meet potential clients and partners, and build valuable business relationships through face-to-face conversations.

The Speaker Hall: Hear Directly from the People Shaping the Industry

The most valuable industry insights often come from those who have built businesses, navigated market shifts and helped shape the financial landscape.

At FM Summit London 2026, the Speaker Hall will feature experienced industry leaders sharing perspectives on the evolution and future of financial markets.

Among the highlights is a fireside chat with Lord Peter Cruddas, founder and CEO of CMC Markets, exploring his career, the evolution of retail trading and the industry's future.

The programme also features:

  • Hormoz Faryar, Managing Director of Institutional Sales, ATFX Connect, MEA

  • Andy Ross, Head of Institutional, Kalshi

  • Waqar Chaudry, Managing Director, Global Head of Digital Assets, Standard Chartered Bank

Representing expertise across institutional sales, trading, digital assets and financial markets, the speakers will bring diverse perspectives to the challenges and opportunities shaping the industry.

Beyond the presentations, the Speaker Hall offers a chance to engage with fresh ideas, exchange perspectives and continue meaningful industry conversations throughout the summit.

Business Connect Roundtables: Where Industry Challenges Meet Candid Discussion

Not every valuable conversation happens on stage. The Business Connect Roundtables at FM Summit London 2026 offer curated, invite-only discussions led by experienced chairs, creating a space for industry professionals to exchange insights and address key business challenges.

The discussions will cover a range of timely industry topics, including digital assets, prediction markets, market liquidity, payments and stablecoins, AI for traders and brokers, the future of funded firms, the role of the UK in retail trading, marketing and answer engine optimisation (AEO), offshore versus onshore licensing, and tokenisation.

These focused discussions encourage practical knowledge-sharing, fresh perspectives and meaningful professional connections. Participation is subject to the programme’s invitation and selection process, making early registration worthwhile for those interested in joining the conversations.

Choose Your Pass and Secure Your Place

FM Summit London 2026 offers three registration pass options, designed for different professional profiles across the financial markets industry.

  • P1 — Brokers & Prop Firms: Free pass for eligible professionals.

  • P2 — Affiliates & IBs: Free pass for eligible affiliates, introducing brokers and other qualifying industry professionals.

  • P3 — Banks & Service Providers: Early-bird pass for eligible banks, payment providers, technology providers and service providers. Early-bird pricing is available until 24 October 2026.

Attendees should select the pass that best matches their professional profile and check the registration page for the applicable terms and pricing.

title: Ethereum’s four-minute settlement plan could lower the cost of moving crypto
summary: A new draft targets a fourfold cut in the time it takes Ethereum transactions to become final, which could free up money transfer services tie up while customers’ payments clear.
content:
Oct 22, 2026, 8:14 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Ethereum researchers have proposed cutting transaction finality from about 16 minutes to roughly four minutes, though the unfinished plan has no activation date.
  • Faster finality could reduce costs for cross-chain transfer services by allowing them to recover and reuse funds more quickly.
  • The proposal would separate validators’ block-selection and finality votes, potentially enabling further speed gains and an eventual shift to quantum-resistant signatures.

Ethereum researchers want to cut the wait for a transaction to become final from about 16 minutes to roughly four, a change that could make it cheaper to move money between blockchains.

Ben Edgington, who coordinates Ethereum’s fast-finality research, filed the draft Wednesday with fellow researchers Francesco D’Amato, Roberto Saltini, Yann Vonlanthen and Mikhail Kalinin.

Its initial target is a four-fold improvement, though the design is unfinished and has no activation date.

In the current mechanism, a transaction can land in an Ethereum block well before the network treats it as final, the point where validators, the computers that secure the network, commit to never rewriting it. Anyone moving funds off Ethereum has to decide when it’s safe to release money on the other side.

But sixteen minutes is a long time to have money in limbo.

Say someone sends $10,000 from Ethereum to another network. A transfer service can pay them right away from money it already holds there, then wait to get repaid once the original transaction settles. The customer gets their funds in seconds, and the service has $10,000 tied up until Ethereum is done.

Ethereum Foundation research counts that idle money as a real cost for these firms, and a shorter wait lets them reuse it sooner. In practice, a service fronting a steady $1 million an hour would have about $267,000 waiting on repayment with a 16-minute delay. At four minutes, however, that drops to roughly $67,000.

Stablecoin providers such as Circle CRCL$86.62·Market Closed, which issues the dollar-pegged USDC, already charges for speed. Its fast route from Ethereum currently costs 0.01%, or $1 per $10,000, before network and application charges. Its standard route carries no Circle transfer fee.

Circle also caps the total value of fast transfers waiting on final settlement, and each completed settlement frees up room for new ones.

Splitting the vote

The 16-minute wait comes down to how Ethereum’s validators vote. Each one casts a single vote that does two jobs at once, helping pick the next block and helping lock older blocks in for good. Validators take turns casting those votes, and a block only becomes final after two full rounds of everyone voting.

Both jobs share one vote so finality can only move as fast as that rotation. The proposal gives each job its own vote, so the locking-in can run on a faster clock that developers can keep tightening over time.

The researchers say splitting the votes would also make it easier to eventually swap in quantum-resistant signatures. Ethereum would need that upgrade if quantum computers ever get strong enough to break today’s cryptography.

However, four minutes would still be slow next to Solana, which switched on its Alpenglow upgrade Wednesday with a target of finality in about 150 milliseconds.

The draft leaves voting timings, penalties and parts of its security analysis unresolved as of Thursday. Edgington wrote that “many aspects remain TBD” and that the immediate aim was getting a proposal number — which puts the idea into Ethereum’s formal upgrade pipeline.

title: Travala Introduces AVA Buyback Multiplier, Scaling Buybacks Up to 4x Member Rewards
summary: Singapore, Singapore, 22nd October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Singapore, Singapore, 22nd October 2026, Chainwire

Singapore, Singapore, October 22nd, 2026, Chainwire

Travala’s monthly AVA Strategic Reserve buyback will now match up to 3x the AVA rewards earned by AVA Smart members

Travala, the Binance-backed crypto travel booking platform, and the AVA Foundation—Travala’s loyalty program provider and issuer of the platform’s native AVA token—today announced the AVA Buyback Multiplier, an upgrade to the AVA Strategic Reserve launched in September 2026. 

Under the new structure, Travala’s monthly match of the AVA Foundation’s buyback scales with the AVA giveback rewards earned by AVA Smart members for booking travel, rising from 1x to up to 3x and taking total monthly buybacks to up to four times member givebacks.

Each month, the AVA Foundation buys back the AVA given to AVA Smart members as booking rewards in the previous month and returns it to its rewards pool. To date, the AVA Foundation has bought back 5,423,181 AVA through its monthly buybacks. Travala matches the monthly amount and moves it into the AVA Strategic Reserve, a multi-signature wallet Travala has committed never to sell or transfer from. Since the AVA Strategic Reserve launched in September, Travala has matched two monthly buybacks, and the reserve now holds 598,458.78 AVA.

Under the AVA Buyback Multiplier, the previous month’s AVA givebacks set Travala’s matched AVA buyback amount. Below $100,000 in monthly AVA givebacks, Travala matches 1x. The match rises to 1.5x at $100,000, 2x at $150,000, 2.5x at $200,000, and a maximum of 3x at $250,000 and above. This brings potential total monthly AVA buybacks to four times monthly AVA Smart member givebacks.

If monthly AVA givebacks fall below a target, the match returns to the lower level the following month. All AVA buybacks by Travala and the AVA Foundation are reported monthly and are verifiable on-chain.

“The AVA Buyback Multiplier ties AVA even more closely to our members’ travel bookings,” said Steve Hipwell, Lead Ecosystem Contributor at AVA Foundation. “Every booking that earns AVA giveback rewards now counts towards the next step up, and every token Travala buys back is permanently locked away in the AVA Strategic Reserve multi-signature custody wallet.”

“We want AVA’s tokenomics to be simple, transparent, and built around real activity,” he continued. “The Buyback Multiplier gives the Smart member community clear milestones to work towards, with every step published on-chain.”

The Buyback Multiplier follows the AVA Smart Program lock update and the launch of the Travala AI Agent on BNB Chain announced earlier this month.

About Travala

Travala founded in 2017 and now backed by industry giant Binance, is the leading crypto-native travel booking service, offering 2,200,000+ properties across 230 countries, 600+ airlines, 50,000+ car rental locations, and 400,000+ activities globally. Travala is a champion of cryptocurrency adoption, accepting over 100 leading cryptocurrencies alongside traditional payment methods. For more information, visit: www.travala.com.

About the AVA Foundation

The AVA Foundation oversees the AVA token ecosystem, including the AVA Smart Program, AVA token, and Travel Tiger NFTs. The AVA token functions as the key to accessing the AVA Smart Program, which provides travel perks and other benefits to Travala customers, such as AVA payment discounts and AVA loyalty rewards. AVA tokenises the concept of loyalty reward programs using blockchain technology, bringing web3 to traditional loyalty models. For more information, visit: www.avafoundation.org. 

Disclaimer

Travala may modify, suspend or discontinue the AVA Buyback Multiplier and future monthly purchases at any time. AVA already in the AVA Strategic Reserve remains subject to the never-sell commitment. This announcement is for information only and does not constitute financial advice, an offer to buy or sell any digital asset, or an inducement to acquire, hold or lock AVA. References to Travala are to TravelFront and its group companies. This announcement is not directed at persons in the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates or any jurisdictions where distribution would be unlawful.

title: Southeast Asia’s Broker Boom Comes with a Catch
summary: Southeast Asia is becoming a more attractive location for retail brokers, with new market entrants launching locally, obtaining licences or establishing regional offices, established brokers expanding their products, marketing, partnerships and local-language services, and more retail investors ente...
content:
2026-10-22T14:00:00.000+02:00

Thursday, 22/10/2026 | 12:00 GMT by Paul Golden

  • Paul Golden explores how rising retail investor numbers are drawing global brokers to Southeast Asia, with Indonesia, Vietnam and the Philippines offering growth opportunities.
  • Indonesia’s retail investor base has topped 20 million, while 49% of Thai investors use trading apps. Yet rising costs, tighter margins and regulatory barriers threaten brokers’ growth.

Southeast Asia is becoming a more attractive location for retail brokers, with new market entrants launching locally, obtaining licences or establishing regional offices, established brokers expanding their products, marketing, partnerships and local-language services, and more retail investors entering financial markets.

London's trading industry is coming home!

But although there is evidence of expanding demand and new international interest, there are also indications that growth is uneven across market segments.

Global Brokers Chase Southeast Asia’s Growing Investor Base

A March 2026 report by The Straits Times found that Indonesia's retail investor population had risen from 3.9 million in 2020 to more than 20 million. It identified Robinhood, South Korea's Hanwha Investment & Securities and Singapore-headquartered Doo Financial as being among the international firms expanding or seeking opportunities in the market.

Robinhood announced in December 2025 that it would acquire two Indonesian businesses to establish a local presence, and its initial target was to complete the transactions in the first half of 2026. However, the acquisitions have not been publicly confirmed as completed, and the reported target for a full local app launch is now early 2027.

A September 2026 survey of 1,200 consumers across Indonesia, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines and Vietnam found that two-thirds already invested and another 26% planned to start within 12 months.

Investment and trading apps are the primary channel for 49% of investors in Thailand, 48% in Indonesia and 44% in Singapore. The most striking contrast lies in the rise of digital wallets and super apps, with 31% of investors in the Philippines primarily managing their investments through a digital wallet or super app, compared with just 3% in Singapore.

Rising incomes, urbanisation and the growth of the middle class are expanding the pool of people able to invest. Younger consumers are also more comfortable using digital platforms and exploring assets beyond traditional savings products.

Indonesia is particularly attractive because of its population size and rapid growth in retail investor numbers. Vietnam and the Philippines offer other sizeable markets, although their regulatory and commercial conditions differ.

In June, Neil Pabari, executive director, retail sales and distribution, Asia Pacific, for CME Group, noted that while young investors in the region are putting money into more traditional assets – such as equities and bonds – they are also showing an openness to alternative assets.

Around three-quarters of cryptocurrency investors in Indonesia are between 18 and 35, according to the Commodity Futures Trading Regulatory Agency. In Malaysia, younger investors are also more likely than older generations to hold alternative assets, with almost a quarter of both Gen Z and millennials holding cryptocurrency.

Pabari observed that retail participation in CME Group markets from the wider Asia Pacific region has grown 16% over the last five years, with heightened regional activity this year in precious metals and oil futures.

Trading Apps and Younger Investors Drive Demand

App-based onboarding, digital identity verification, electronic payments and low minimum deposits make it easier to acquire and serve customers without a large branch network. This benefits both local stockbrokers and international forex, CFD and multi-asset brokers.

Technology also makes it easier to serve customers across borders, although it does not remove local licensing requirements.

Social media and trading communities are also improving customer acquisition. Younger prospective traders are discovering platforms through online communities, influencers, educational content and peer recommendations. This is enabling brokers to target customers by language, country and trading interests without relying solely on traditional advertising.

Retail investors increasingly want access to overseas equities, indices, commodities, currencies and crypto-related products. Brokers can compete by offering broader market access, different account types, more sophisticated platforms and local funding options.

For FX and CFD brokers in particular, the opportunity is not just to attract first-time traders: it is also to win active clients from established competitors through tighter pricing, better execution and more reliable withdrawals.

Singapore provides a useful example of the overlap and the distinction between these businesses. The MAS capital markets licensing framework covers securities, exchange-traded derivatives, OTC derivatives and leveraged foreign exchange trading, subject to applicable licensing requirements and exemptions.

In other countries, the regulatory treatment of leveraged FX trading can be more restrictive. Thailand's central bank, for example, states that retail speculative FX trading through platforms or websites is not currently permitted under its foreign exchange framework.

The Indonesian moves reported this year illustrate the attraction of establishing a presence in a fast-growing market. They also show why it is important to distinguish a proposed entry from an operational launch.

Growth Comes with Regulatory and Commercial Pressures

Of course, the opportunity is not uniformly attractive. A Deloitte Thailand study published earlier this year refers to a brokerage industry under sustained pressure from declining trading volumes, prolonged margin compression, rising operating costs and rapid shifts in investor behaviour.

These challenges are occurring within a broader capital market context marked by weakened investor confidence, a limited pipeline of high-quality issuers and an underdeveloped private capital ecosystem.

As a result, many brokerage firms – particularly mid-sized and smaller players – are struggling to invest in technology, product innovation, governance and investor engagement at the required scale to remain competitive.

According to Deloitte, the current level of fragmentation, operating within a finite profit pool, has constrained profitability and inhibited reinvestment across much of the sector. Consolidation can therefore play an important role in strengthening balance sheets, improving operational efficiency and enabling investment in scale-dependent capabilities.

So while international brokers want access to new retail customers and local firms are developing digital offerings, established firms may merge, be acquired or leave markets where customer acquisition and compliance costs are too high.

title: Crypto traders seek shelter in bitcoin as altcoins slide and ETF flows wobble
summary: Your day-ahead look for Oct. 21, 2026
content:
Oct 22, 2026, 7:20 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

This is an excerpt from CoinDesk newsletter 'Daybook.' Sign up here, if you haven't already.

Bitcoin’s BTC$84,459.46 share of the crypto market has climbed to the highest level since May, even as prices across the wider market weaken.

The cryptocurrency’s dominance rate, its contribution to the total market value of digital assets, reached 60% on Wednesday and remains near that level. The move signals a renewed preference for BTC, with investors favoring the largest cryptocurrency over alternative coins.

The rise in dominance comes amid muted price action. Bitcoin slipped below $82,000 on Thursday, reversing Wednesday’s brief push above $84,000. On a seven-day basis, BTC and most other major tokens — including ether ETH$2,490.55, XRP (XRP) and solana (SOL) — were largely little changed to positive, with zcash (ZEC) the only major coin to advance more than 10%.

Smaller tokens, however, have seen bigger declines. The CoinDesk Memecoin Index fell more than 5%, while the CoinDesk Computing Select Index dropped 3.5% and the DeFi Select Index lost 2.5%.

Analysts say the market is awaiting a fresh catalyst.

“The earlier period of crypto outperformance has given way to closer alignment with equities as investors wait for a fresh catalyst within the sector,” Joel Kruger, a market strategist at LMAX Group said in an email.

Kruger added that global macroeconomic situation remains the dominant influence, and bitcoin’s scarcity could help it sustain potential jitters in global equity markets.

Vikram Subburaj, CEO of India-based Giottus exchange, cautioned against chasing bitcoin rallies, pointing out that exchange-traded funds (ETFs) still lack a consistent bid.

“Flows remain volatile, and sustained inflows are needed to confirm a stronger recovery,” he said in an email. “Our advice: Investors should avoid chasing short-term rallies. Consider staggered entries, maintain measured position sizes and monitor ETF flows and Fed signals before increasing exposure.”

The Federal Reserve is set to meet on interest-rate policy next week. Stay alert!

Read more: For analysis of today's activity in altcoins and derivatives, see Crypto Markets Today . For a comprehensive list of events this week, see CoinDesk's "Crypto Week Ahead."

What’s trending

  • Asian stocks tumble, bitcoin retreats as China enters bear market (CoinDesk): Equities slumped as technology shares sank and rising oil prices compounded investor concerns.
  • China seeks to seize 61,800 BTC tied to $5.7 billion fraud scheme (CoinDesk): Chinese prosecutors moved to seize more than 61,800 bitcoin linked to a fraud case worth roughly $5.7 billion, days after a U.K. court ruled Chinese law governs victims’ claims to the coins.
  • Yen set for biggest rally in a month; risk-averse investors shun dollar (Reuters): The yen headed for its strongest daily rally in a month, drawing ​safe-haven flows from investors fretting over fragile equity markets, high crude prices, war in the Middle East and potential disappointment in future ‌returns from AI.
  • World’s largest wealth fund posts $30 billion loss after bond market turbulence (CNBC): Norway’s sovereign wealth fund said its investment portfolio lost $30 billion in the third quarter as rising interest rates dented returns on its bond holdings. The period saw a global bond market rout as major central banks began raising interest rates and concerns about inflation and government debt mounted.

Today’s signal

The chart shows XRP’s daily price swings since May. Overlaid on the chart is the Ichimoku cloud, an indicator used to identify support, resistance and momentum.

XRP is currently trading below the cloud, a sign of bearish momentum building. Crossovers above and below the cloud are said to represent bullish and bearish trend reversals.

The graphic indicates that if prices hold below the cloud, further losses may follow.

title: Pudgy Penguins (PENGU) Price Prediction: Bullish SuperTrend Flip Signals Potential 70% Rally to $0.013
summary: Pudgy Penguins (PENGU) is showing a fresh bullish signal on its 12-hour chart, drawing attention to a possible recovery toward $0.013.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: PENGU

Pudgy Penguins (PENGU) is showing a fresh bullish signal on its 12-hour chart, drawing attention to a possible recovery toward $0.013.

The technical setup comes as PENGU trades near $0.0081 and approaches a key breakout zone.

Crypto analyst Ali Charts highlighted a bullish SuperTrend flip, noting that previous changes in the indicator’s direction had coincided with rallies and corrections. However, the signal does not guarantee another advance, and PENGU must overcome several resistance levels before a sustained recovery can be confirmed.

PENGU SuperTrend Flip Raises Bullish Price Prediction

Ali Charts identified the bullish SuperTrend signal as PENGU moved above $0.0081. The indicator is commonly used to assess market direction by comparing price action with a volatility-based trend line. A bullish flip can indicate improving momentum, while a bearish flip may signal weakening price conditions.

PENGU’s 12-hour chart shows a bullish SuperTrend flip above $0.0081, signaling potential upside based on the indicator’s historical trend-reversal signals. Source: @alicharts via X

The analyst also referred to an earlier TD Sequential analysis that identified buy signals preceding gains of 77% and 67%. A previous sell signal was followed by a 32% decline according to the post. These historical moves provide context for the latest signal, but they do not establish that PENGU will repeat the same performance.

Based on the possibility of another rally of roughly 70%, the analyst pointed to $0.013 as a potential upside target. From a price near $0.0081, that level would represent an increase of approximately 60%, rather than a full 70% gain. A 70% advance from $0.0081 would put the token near $0.0138.

The distinction matters because technical targets depend on the precise entry price and the size of the projected move. Traders will also need to monitor trading volume, resistance, and broader cryptocurrency market conditions to assess whether the bullish signal is gaining strength.

Symmetrical Triangle Puts PENGU Breakout in Focus

A separate TradingView analysis by CryptoNuclear identifies a tightening symmetrical triangle on PENGU’s four-day chart. The pattern has developed as the token records lower highs while maintaining progressively higher lows, narrowing the range in which it trades.

PENGU has formed a symmetrical triangle since peaking near $0.0466, with lower highs and rising support compressing the price range toward a potential breakout. Source: CryptoNuclear on TradingView

The structure reflects a market in which sellers continue to limit upward moves, while buyers attempt to defend higher support levels. As the two trend lines converge, the token approaches a point where a decisive move may become more likely. The pattern alone, however, does not indicate which direction the breakout will take.

PENGU previously reached a peak near $0.0466 before entering a prolonged decline and consolidation phase. With the token trading around $0.0081 in the supplied chart analysis, a recovery would need to overcome several overhead resistance zones to demonstrate that buying pressure is returning.

CryptoNuclear’s analysis emphasizes confirmation rather than anticipation. A sustained move above descending resistance, supported by stronger trading volume and a successful retest, would provide better evidence of a bullish breakout. A brief move above the trend line without follow-through could instead prove to be a false breakout.

PENGU Price Prediction: Key Resistance Levels and Bullish Targets

The four-day chart identifies $0.0105 as the first resistance level to watch. A move above this threshold could strengthen the recovery setup, although PENGU would still face additional barriers before reaching the $0.013 area highlighted by Ali Charts.

PENGU’s daily chart flashes a TD Sequential buy signal after previous signals preceded gains of 77.64% and 66.94%. Source: Ali Martinez via X

The next resistance levels are $0.0127 and $0.0150. The former sits close to the projected $0.013 target, making it an important level for evaluating whether bullish momentum can persist. A sustained break above $0.0150 would offer further evidence that the recovery is extending beyond an initial rebound.

If the token clears these intermediate barriers, the chart identifies $0.0232 and $0.0268 as more distant potential targets. Those levels would require a substantially larger advance and should be treated as conditional scenarios rather than near-term expectations.

The following levels summarize the main areas identified in the supplied technical analyses:

  • Initial resistance: $0.0105
  • Intermediate resistance: $0.0127
  • Key recovery threshold: $0.0150
  • Higher resistance zone: $0.0232
  • Extended bullish target: $0.0268
  • SuperTrend signal reference price: $0.0081
  • Potential support: $0.0065
  • Lower support zone: $0.0050–0.0037

These levels are based on the supplied chart analyses and may change as price action develops. They are not guaranteed points of reversal or continuation.

PENGU Price Prediction: Higher Highs and Higher Lows Support Recovery Case

Another technical analysis shared by @0xSweep points to a sequence of higher highs and higher lows on PENGU’s daily chart. This pattern can indicate that buyers are gradually gaining control, provided the token continues to defend its recent swing lows.

$PENGU is forming higher highs and higher lows on its daily chart, forecasting a potential 20%+ rally if Bitcoin holds above $83K. Source: @0xSweep via X

The analyst suggested that PENGU could gain more than 20% if Bitcoin holds above $83,000. Such a move would depend on both the token’s chart structure and conditions across the broader cryptocurrency market. Bitcoin weakness could undermine the setup by reducing risk appetite for smaller crypto assets.

Higher highs and higher lows are useful measures of price structure, but they do not confirm that an uptrend will continue indefinitely. A break below a previous higher low would weaken the bullish interpretation, while a move above a recent swing high could strengthen it.

The chart shows prolonged sideways consolidation after the latest down-wave failed to trigger a new up-wave, leaving the market awaiting a decisive breakout or breakdown. Source: MasterAnanda on TradingView

The longer-term outlook remains less certain. A separate TradingView analysis by MasterAnanda describes PENGU as having spent an extended period consolidating after its earlier decline. The analysis interprets the rising long-term support structure as a potential foundation for another bullish cycle, although the duration and scale of any recovery remain unknown.

PENGU Bearish Scenario: $0.0065 Support Remains Important

Despite the bullish SuperTrend flip, PENGU has not confirmed a sustained breakout from its broader consolidation pattern. Failure to overcome descending resistance could leave the token vulnerable to another pullback.

The four-day chart identifies $0.0065 as an important potential support area. A decline toward this level would indicate that sellers had regained control of the short-term trend. If support breaks, the $0.0050–$0.0037 region becomes a lower zone to monitor, according to the supplied chart analysis.

A convincing bearish signal would involve a close below ascending trendline support, preferably accompanied by rising selling volume. Such a move would weaken the argument that PENGU is establishing progressively higher lows.

Broader market conditions also matter. A decline in Bitcoin or a wider retreat across speculative crypto assets could increase selling pressure on PENGU, regardless of its individual technical indicators. title: Standard Chartered Buys 100% of Zodia Custody
summary:

The post Standard Chartered Buys 100% of Zodia Custody appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Standard Chartered entered into definitive agreements to acquire 100 per cent of Zodia Custody UK Limited.
  • The five regulated Zodia crypto custody businesses in key markets will be consolidated into the Securities Services segment of Standard Chartered.
  • The software and professional services division of Zodia will be split into a new company called Zodia Solutions.

The lender will extend its offerings of institutional crypto services by standardizing Custodian’s Zodia offering, which will be integrated into its platform. The deal remains subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.

  • Standard Chartered Takes Full Control of Zodia Custody
  • Zodia Custody Becomes Part of a Global Banking Platform
    • Zodia Solutions Will Separate From the Custody Business
    • Standard Chartered Expands Its Institutional Crypto Stack

Standard Chartered Takes Full Control of Zodia Custody

Standard Chartered I H Limited will purchase the 100% of Zodia’s regulated operating businesses held in Zodia Custody UK Limited. They currently serve clients at locations in Singapore, Hong Kong, Australia, United Arab Emirates and Luxembourg.

In closing the sale, the regulated digital asset custody operations will be fully amalgamated with Standard Chartered’s current securities services operations.

The move is meant to streamline the bank’s crypto-asset custody operation and to provide a more cohesive offering to institutional customers spanning both traditional securities and crypto assets, the bank said.

Read More: Standard Chartered Launches Bitcoin and Ether Spot Trading for UAE Institutions

Zodia Custody Becomes Part of a Global Banking Platform

The acquisition details provide Standard Chartered with a crypto custody service that it controls directly in regulated markets in various financial hubs. The insurance of digital-assets is propelling custody into the traditional banking system, said Zodia Custody CEO Richard Clark.

The integration of Zodia’s expertise and systems with SCh’s global banking network is thought to deepen regulatory custody services for institutional clients. All current Zodia Custody customers will be expected to receive services during the transaction without interruption.

Zodia Solutions Will Separate From the Custody Business

The custody integration will not cover Zodia’s software or professional services. Rather than that, those assets will be handed over to a new independent business called ‘Zodia Solutions’, which was created under SC Ventures.

For financial institutions seeking to launch and grow crypto-related services, Zodia Solutions will be dedicated to providing them with bank-grade digital asset technology.

A team of banking and investment partners will also support the entity comprising NAB Ventures, Northern Trust, SBI Ventures Asset, Emirates NBD, Investcorp related entities and others. Standard Chartered will continue to be one of the institutions that will utilize the technology.

Standard Chartered Expands Its Institutional Crypto Stack

The Zodia acquisition dovetails into Standard Chartered’s expanding list of digital asset services which include custody.

The bank is targeting to integrate digital assets into its broader securities platform, providing access to digital assets for institutional clients via a platform connected to a recognized global bank.

The decision also signals a wider trend for crypto custody and infrastructure services across the financial sector instead of conducting small-scale pilots to investigate cryptocurrencies.

For Standard Chartered, owning Zodia Custody gives it direct control over a regulated digital asset custody network while Zodia Solutions continues operating as a separate technology provider for banks entering the crypto market.

title: Tether Backs Peso to Expand USDT Payments Across 4 Major Latin American Markets

content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Tether led the pre-seed investment of Bolivian fintech Peso for the growing USDT payment infrastructure.
  • Today Peso is used to facilitate USDT on QR payments, banking rails, virtual accounts and food delivery.
  • The funds will drive growth in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia and Argentina.

Tether has driven USDT further into daily payments in Latin America. The stablecoin’s issuer has led a pre-seed funding round for Bolivian fintech Peso to facilitate quicker connections between USDT, merchants, banking networks, and consumer apps.

Tether Invests in Peso to Expand USD₮ Payment Infrastructure Across Latin America

Read more:

https://t.co/RE6LFFzlNt

— Tether (@tether) October 21, 2026

  • Tether Targets Everyday USDT Payments
  • USDT Connects Crypto Wallets With Local Banking Rails
    • Peso Plans Expansion Across Four Markets
    • Tether Deepens USDT’s Role in Latin America

Tether Targets Everyday USDT Payments

The Peso application combines saving, spending, investing, cross-border transfers and facilitates user access to a USDT account across the world. The company is also developing the USDT infrastructure to move beyond crypto wallets and into services that the consumers are already using.

For instance, Peso has partnered with Yango in Bolivia, enabling platform users to place food orders and make payments directly within the app using USDT.

Peso also facilitates merchant point-of-sale transactions and virtual accounts that have been registered under consumers’ names. These accounts provide the ability to swap between USDT and Bolivian local currency via QR and ACH rails, enabling customers to transfer between stablecoins and local currency. Tether provided no details on how big the investment would be.

Read More: Tether Celebrates 12 Years, USD₮ Surpasses 700M Users

USDT Connects Crypto Wallets With Local Banking Rails

The focus of the deal is on the simplicity of the usage of USDT and does not require any payment network to be abandoned by the user. Peso’s model connects stablecoin balances with local financial infrastructure instead of limiting USDT to crypto-native transactions.

This renders it possible for a user to carry USDT, pay a business, transport funds from one nation to another, or push funds into native banking channels from the identical machine. The investment is meant to back infrastructure that allows USDT to become a payments tool in everyday life, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said.

Peso Plans Expansion Across Four Markets

With the new funding, Peso is expanding on-ramps and off-ramps in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia and Argentina. The company will use USDT as a settlement channel to link up various local currencies, and also develop its own Merchant solutions.

There will be further investments in POS infrastructure and expanded virtualization services for both customer and business users. The investment aligns with a broader strategy for Tether to back payments platforms that connect the old economy with blockchain payments.

Not just the trading of crypto assets, the company is supporting infrastructure for retail buying, e-commerce, transportation, banking access and cross-border transfers.

Read More: Tether Freezes $1.45M in THORChain USDT Vaults, Reverses Blacklist Hours Later

Tether Deepens USDT’s Role in Latin America

Dollar-linked stablecoins have emerged as one of the attractive solutions for securing stable value with quicker onboarding and settling across borders for users in Latin America.

Many users are already holding USDT in this region while what has been lacking is the ease of infrastructure to spend USDT in daily life, Peso CEO and co-founder Alejandro Terán said.

With Tether now backing the company, Peso plans to accelerate that rollout across multiple markets and make USDT usable through QR payments, merchant systems, digital services, and local banking connections.

title: Cardano Pushes Back on EU MiCA Expansion for DeFi, Staking and Crypto Lending
summary:
Key Takeaways: The Cardano Foundation advocated against the EU coming up with new rules for DeFi, staking, lending, or protocol-level crypto activities. The group is not interested in the regulation
The post Cardano Pushes Back on EU MiCA Expansion for DeFi, Staking and Crypto Lending appeared first...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The Cardano Foundation advocated against the EU coming up with new rules for DeFi, staking, lending, or protocol-level crypto activities.
  • The group is not interested in the regulation of blockchain, but the regulation based on the economic function, control and risk.
  • Cardano further urged for more clearly defined MiCA borders, greater uniformity across the EU, and reduced legal overlaps of current financial regulations.

The Cardano Foundation is urging European regulators to keep MiCA narrowly scoped and prevent overly broad classification of all decentralized crypto-related activities as separately regulated services.

In its response to the European Commission’s MiCA review, the Foundation argued that more regulation would not automatically make Europe’s crypto market safer or more competitive.

  • Cardano Opposes New MiCA Rules for DeFi and Staking
  • Cardano Draws a Line Between Staking and Custodial Services
    • MiCA Boundaries Need More Clarity, Not More Categories

Cardano Opposes New MiCA Rules for DeFi and Staking

The Foundation’s submission was made to the Commission on September 30, 2026 and was targeted at topics that are pertinent to public and permissionless blockchains. The simplistic message of its position is that regulation must focus on what the activity is, who is controlling the activity, and what are the risks presented by the activity.

That means that DeFi, staking, lending, and more blockchain-based activities should not be subjected to new regulations simply because they run on decentralized infrastructure.

The Foundation recommended that regulators move on to named entities that carry out regulated financial activities or have meaningful control of customer transactions and assets.

Read More: Cardano and Injective Launch First Live IBC Link, Connecting ADA and INJ Ecosystems

Cardano Draws a Line Between Staking and Custodial Services

One of the clearest examples of this in Cardano’s reply was when they staked. A loner can choose to represent their stake to the very point that they lead the procedure for such consensus of the community without surrendering the property or staking any of their tokens in the middleman.

The Foundation stressed the need for a different approach to such direct protocol interaction than for systems with greater financial ownership concentration or decision-making ability of the company.

It also stated that simple technical access to a decentralized network as well as general purpose blockchain infrastructure and autonomous software are not financial services per se.

MiCA Boundaries Need More Clarity, Not More Categories

Cardano also voted against removing the distinction between MiCA and other financial controls including the MiFID II.

The classification of a crypto asset as a financial instrument should be based on its actual nature, and not its location on a crypto network. The Foundation stated, however, that there was a lack of clarity around hybrid tokens and assets that evolve over time.

It also stated that different national interpretations in EU member states could have an impact on MiCA’s objectives of creating one concerted crypto market.

The Foundation seeks less overlap between MiCA and payment rules, greater clarity for multi-issuer stablecoins and greater practical sustainability disclosure, which takes into account differences between the designs of blockchains.

Cardano additionally voiced opposition to the automatic classification of NFTs, crypto lending, perpetual futures and prediction markets for the new MiCa-specific categories.

title: Bitcoin Price Prediction: Michael Saylor Says BTC Will Reach $100K in 12 Months as 4-Year Bull Run Begins
summary: Bitcoin price prediction discussions have gained fresh attention after Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor forecast that BTC could return to $100,000 within the next 12 months.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin price prediction discussions have gained fresh attention after Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor forecast that BTC could return to $100,000 within the next 12 months.

Speaking on the Schwab Network, Saylor said the cryptocurrency was entering a new bull market and predicted that the broader rally could last four years. His outlook comes as Bitcoin trades near $83,700, with technical indicators showing a positive trend but mixed short-term momentum.

Saylor’s forecast reflects his long-standing confidence in Bitcoin’s limited supply and its potential role in financial markets. However, the $100,000 target remains a projection rather than a confirmed outcome. Monetary policy, institutional demand, regulatory developments, and market liquidity could all influence the cryptocurrency’s next move.

Key Facts

  • Bitcoin price prediction: Saylor expects BTC to return above $100,000 within the next 12 months but did not guarantee that the target would be reached by the end of 2026.
  • Four-year bull market: The Strategy executive chairman described the current phase as the beginning of a bull run that could last four years.
  • Current BTC price: Bitcoin was trading around $83,700 in the supplied market snapshot, leaving it approximately 19.4% below $100,000.
  • Strategy’s Bitcoin holdings: The company reported holdings of 848,517 BTC, alongside approximately $5.2 billion in cash reserves, according to the supplied source report.
  • Technical outlook: TradingView’s technical summary indicated a Buy rating, supported by moving averages, while oscillators remained broadly neutral.
  • Corporate strategy: Strategy is pursuing a proposal for daily dividend payments on its credit instruments, with a shareholder vote scheduled for October 28.

Bitcoin Clears Its 200-Week Average as Headwinds Fade

Saylor said Bitcoin had rebounded from its 200-week moving average and climbed approximately $20,000 above that level. He views the recovery as evidence that the previous downturn has run its course and that the market may be entering a new expansion phase.

“I feel like we’re at the beginning of a bull run,” Saylor told the Schwab Network. He also said he expected Bitcoin to return to six-figure valuations within 12 months, while acknowledging that he could not be certain it would happen before the end of 2026. When asked how long the bull market might last, he replied, “Four years.”

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The forecast comes as Bitcoin remains below its October 2025 all-time high of approximately $126,198, according to the supplied market report. At around $83,700, BTC would need to gain roughly 19.4% to reclaim $100,000. A move to that level would represent a meaningful recovery, although it would not establish a new record.

Saylor attributed recent market pressure to restrictive monetary, foreign, and trade policies, alongside competition for investment capital from artificial intelligence. He argued that these forces had weighed on Bitcoin without necessarily undermining its underlying investment case.

He also pointed to the potential expansion of Bitcoin-backed lending, regulatory guidance from US financial authorities, and the development of tokenized securities as factors that could support wider adoption. These developments could improve access to digital assets, although their effect on Bitcoin’s price will depend on actual demand and market conditions.

Bitcoin Price Prediction: What Technical Indicators Show

The TradingView snapshot placed BTC near $83,729, with the overall technical assessment at Buy. Moving averages were classified as Strong Buy, while oscillators remained Neutral. This combination suggests that the prevailing trend is constructive, but short-term momentum has not confirmed a strong breakout.

A close above $83,600 could push the price toward $84,000, while a drop below $83,300 may trigger a pullback toward the $82,950 point of control (POC). Source: kenkemdayfx on TradingView

Bitcoin was trading above several short- and medium-term moving averages, including the 10-period exponential moving average near $82,519 and the 20-period exponential moving average around $82,613. The 50-period EMA stood near $80,733, while the 200-period EMA was approximately $76,071. These levels provide reference points for assessing whether the recent recovery remains intact.

The relative strength index was around 54, a neutral reading that does not indicate an overbought market. The Average Directional Index was near 19, suggesting limited trend strength. Together, these indicators point to a market with a positive moving-average structure but without decisive confirmation of accelerating momentum.

Key price levels also offer a framework for monitoring the BTC price. The $82,000–$83,000 area forms an important near-term support zone, while resistance begins around $84,700 and extends toward $89,000. A sustained move above this resistance region could strengthen the case for a continued recovery. Conversely, a breakdown below the support cluster could expose lower levels, including the mid-$70,000 range.

Saylor Calls the CLARITY Act a Bill of Restrictions

Saylor also discussed the stalled CLARITY Act, a proposed US legislative framework for digital assets. He argued that the legislation placed excessive emphasis on restrictions rather than establishing clear permissions for innovation.

“If you want to create a great economy or a great nation, what you want is a bill of rights, not a bill of restrictions,” Saylor said during the interview. He criticized the proposal’s length and argued that its provisions would have imposed substantial constraints on the digital asset industry.

Michael Saylor argues that the CLARITY Act’s potential failure could benefit Bitcoin by reducing regulatory uncertainty and allowing the market to develop in ways that support a stronger bull run. Source: @AltcoinDaily via X

Instead, Saylor pointed to guidance and initiatives involving the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, and the US Treasury. He said developments involving tokenization, digital derivatives, and digital currency issuance could provide a more favorable environment for financial innovation.

Regulatory clarity can influence institutional participation by helping businesses understand the rules governing custody, trading, issuance, and other digital asset activities. However, the precise effects on Bitcoin demand will depend on how policies are implemented and whether they encourage additional investment.

Saylor also emphasized monetary policy as a central influence on financial markets. Lower borrowing costs and improved liquidity can support demand for risk assets, while restrictive financial conditions may limit investment. Bitcoin remains sensitive to these shifts, despite its fixed maximum supply of 21 million coins.

The distinction matters for the current Bitcoin price prediction. A more supportive regulatory environment may encourage participation, but it cannot guarantee a sustained rally if liquidity tightens or investors reduce exposure to volatile assets.

Strategy’s 845,000 Bitcoin and the Oct. 28 Dividend Vote

Strategy’s substantial Bitcoin holdings remain central to Saylor’s long-term outlook. The company’s reported position of 848,517 BTC, valued at roughly $70 billion at the prices cited in the source report, makes it one of the largest corporate holders of the cryptocurrency. Its cash reserves of approximately $5.2 billion provide additional financial resources as the company manages its capital structure.

Saylor said Strategy had acquired approximately 160,000 BTC during 2026, describing the company as the world’s largest Bitcoin buyer. Its approach, however, extends beyond simply accumulating and holding the asset. Strategy also manages equity and credit instruments to support its financing activities and maintain access to capital.

That approach is particularly relevant to the company’s preferred securities, including STRC. These instruments form part of Strategy’s digital credit strategy, which Saylor views as an important component of its broader business model. Their performance and liquidity can influence financing costs and the company’s ability to continue acquiring Bitcoin.

Shareholders are scheduled to vote on October 28 on a proposal to move dividend payments on certain credit instruments to a daily calendar-day schedule. Saylor said the proposed securities would be the first in the world to pay dividends every calendar day. The plan is intended to align payments more closely with digital markets that operate around the clock, including weekends and holidays.

Daily distributions could change how investors manage cash flows and trade these securities. However, the proposal’s approval, implementation, and eventual effect on trading behavior remain important considerations.

Strategy’s financial structure also creates exposure to Bitcoin’s volatility. A rising BTC price can increase the value of its holdings, while a prolonged decline can pressure the company’s market valuation and financing conditions. Its cash reserves and capital-management policies therefore matter alongside the size of its Bitcoin position.

Institutional Forecasts Add Context to Bitcoin’s Long-Term Outlook

Saylor’s bullish outlook comes as traditional financial institutions increasingly examine Bitcoin’s potential role in investment portfolios. J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report, released on October 19, introduced a range of long-term return expectations for Bitcoin. The report assesses asset classes over a 10- to 15-year horizon rather than attempting to predict short-term price movements.

Michael Saylor cites J.P. Morgan’s 10-year forecast, which projects Bitcoin’s 10% annualized return to outperform REITs, stocks, bonds, gold, and cash. Source: Michael Saylor via X

This distinction is important when evaluating Bitcoin predictions. Long-term portfolio assumptions do not establish where BTC will trade over the next 12 months, and they should not be interpreted as confirmation of Saylor’s $100,000 target.

Bitcoin’s limited supply remains central to the investment argument advanced by Saylor. He has argued that artificial intelligence may generate substantial corporate wealth but cannot increase Bitcoin’s predetermined supply. In his view, that scarcity distinguishes BTC from assets whose supply can expand through additional production or issuance.

Even so, scarcity alone does not determine market value. Investor demand, liquidity, regulation, and broader economic conditions remain significant influences on the price of Bitcoin. Institutional participation can support demand, but it can also change as portfolio managers reassess risk.

BTC Price Prediction: Can Bitcoin Reach $100K Within 12 Months?

Bitcoin’s near-term outlook combines a constructive moving-average structure with resistance that the market must overcome. At approximately $83,700, the cryptocurrency needs a gain of about 19.4% to reach $100,000. That move is possible, but the technical indicators supplied do not establish that it will occur within Saylor’s proposed timeframe.

A sustained move above the $84,700–$89,000 resistance area would provide stronger evidence of improving momentum. Beyond that range, traders would monitor whether buying activity remains sufficient to carry BTC toward the psychological $100,000 level. Failure to hold the $82,000–$83,000 support region, meanwhile, could weaken the short-term structure and shift attention toward lower support levels.

Saylor’s four-year bull-market outlook is a longer-term thesis, not a guarantee that Bitcoin will rise continuously. The cryptocurrency could experience sharp corrections even if a broader upward trend develops. Changes in monetary policy, institutional flows, and investor appetite for risk could all influence its path.

For now, the Bitcoin price prediction rests on two distinct considerations: Saylor’s expectation that the next bull market has begun and the market’s ability to confirm that view through sustained price gains. His forecast provides a clear target and timeframe, while technical indicators offer a framework for tracking progress.

Whether BTC reaches $100,000 within 12 months will ultimately depend on market conditions rather than any single executive’s prediction. Investors following the latest Bitcoin price news should distinguish between an optimistic long-term outlook and evidence of a confirmed breakout. Technical indicators and price targets can help frame that assessment, but neither guarantees future performance.

Binance Global vs Binance US

The Binance platform works by acting as a middleman that connects people who want to buy crypto with people who want to sell it. You can easily create an account, deposit funds, and then you use the exchange’s order book to place your trades. The system then uses its matching engine to pair your buy order with someone else’s sell order at the best possible price. Once the trade is complete, the assets are transferred between internal wallets.

You will notice that your account is divided into several sub-wallets based on what you are doing. You have a Spot Wallet for regular buying and holding, a Futures Wallet for leverage trading, and an Earn Wallet for your savings. You can move your money between these wallets instantly and for free. Basically, this structure helps you keep your different trading strategies organized so you don’t accidentally spend your long-term savings on a risky day trade.

  • Multiple Trading Pairs: Binance has over 1,300 trading pairs from which traders can choose. Some of these pairs include BTC/USDT, BTC/FDUSD, XRP/USDT, ETH/USDT,  USDC/USDT, SOL/USDT, and many more.

Additionally, you can get 25% discounts if you use the Binance coin, BNB.

The platform also has many order types, including limit order, market order, stop-limit order, stop market order, trailing stop order, and post-only order.
  • Robust Security and KYC: Binance enforces various security measures to protect users. For instance, the platform requires a strong password during registration and 2FA for all sensitive operations, such as logging in and transferring funds. They also encrypt data in storage and in transit to ensure that only you can access your personal information. Plus, in addition to these measures, Binance has a strict Know-Your-Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) policy.
  • Supports Fiat-to-crypto: Binance users can easily convert their local currency into digital assets. Some supported fiat on Binance include GBP, AUD, BRL, EUR, USD, ZAR, and RUS. You can make these fiat-to-crypto deposits using bank transfers, online banking, e-wallets, credit/debit cards, and Google/Apple Pay.
  • User-Friendly Mobile app: The Binance app is available for iOS and Android with a simplified Lite mode for beginners and an advanced Pro mode for traders. The app also integrates the Web3 wallet, NFTs, and Earn features.

Disadvantages of Binance

In fact, even traders who are familiar with the platform might feel overwhelmed due to all the options available.
  • Lawsuits and Regulatory Trouble in Multiple Countries: Binance has faced many regulatory and legal issues in multiple countries. In November 2023, Binance and its CEO, CZ, pleaded guilty to unlicensed money transmitting and anti-money laundering violations charges. This happened a month after Binance paused all U.S. dollar deposits, withdrawals, and trades in response to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) lawsuit filed against Binance.US on June 5, 2023.
  • Custodial Risk: Although Binance offers self‑custody through its Web3 wallet, most of the users keep their funds on the exchange for trading. In November 2022 and October 2023, there were hacks against the BNB Chain (around $570 million), and earlier in 2019, hackers stole about 7,000 BTC from the exchange. Obviously, Binance covered the losses through the SAFU fund, but these incidents eventually show that even big exchanges are not immune to security breaches.

Who Is Binance Best For?

Binance is best for active day traders, altcoin investors, passive income, high-volume traders, and tech-savvy beginners.
